Mobile manipulators fit naturally within this paradigm because they serve as physical agents capable of bridging digital planning systems and physical production processes. Their ability to move, perceive, manipulate, communicate, and adapt makes them key enablers of future manufacturing ecosystems.</p> <p>Future machine tending systems will likely incorporate Vision-Language Models, Vision-Language-Action architectures, foundation models, and embodied AI technologies. These advances will enable robots to understand high-level production objectives, interpret natural language instructions, adapt to previously unseen machine configurations, and learn new tasks with minimal programming effort. Rather than requiring detailed task-specific engineering, future mobile manipulators may acquire machine tending skills through demonstration, simulation, and autonomous learning.</p> <p>Ultimately, machine tending represents one of the most economically compelling and technologically mature use cases for mobile manipulators. It addresses critical manufacturing challenges related to labor availability, productivity, flexibility, quality, and scalability while leveraging the unique strengths of mobile manipulation technology. By combining autonomous navigation, intelligent perception, adaptive manipulation, industrial connectivity, and artificial intelligence, mobile manipulators transform machine tending from a repetitive support activity into a strategic capability that enhances overall manufacturing performance. As factories continue their transition toward smart, autonomous, and highly flexible production environments, machine tending will remain a foundational application driving the adoption of next-generation mobile manipulation systems.</p> <p>Inspection is one of the most important applications of mobile manipulators because it directly influences product quality, operational safety, regulatory compliance, equipment reliability, and overall business performance. In industrial environments, inspection refers to the systematic process of observing, measuring, analyzing, and verifying the condition of products, machines, facilities, infrastructure, or operational processes. Traditionally, inspection activities have relied heavily on human workers who manually examine products, monitor equipment conditions, record observations, and make judgments regarding quality and maintenance requirements. While human inspectors provide flexibility and experience, manual inspection is often time-consuming, inconsistent, labor-intensive, and subject to fatigue-induced errors. Mobile manipulators offer a transformative alternative by combining autonomous mobility, advanced perception, robotic manipulation, artificial intelligence, and data analytics into a unified platform capable of performing inspection tasks continuously, consistently, and at scale. Inspection has therefore become one of the most strategically important use cases for next-generation mobile manipulation systems.</p> <p>The role of inspection extends across numerous industries including manufacturing, logistics, warehousing, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, food processing, energy production, mining, transportation, aerospace, construction, and public infrastructure management. In each of these domains, inspection serves as a mechanism for detecting abnormalities, ensuring compliance, maintaining quality standards, and preventing failures before they occur. The increasing complexity of modern industrial systems has significantly increased the volume and frequency of inspection activities required. Consequently, organizations are seeking automated solutions capable of providing higher accuracy, improved consistency, and greater operational efficiency than traditional manual approaches.</p> <p>Historically, industrial inspection evolved from visual examinations performed by skilled workers. Inspectors relied primarily on human senses to identify defects, irregularities, damage, contamination, wear, corrosion, or process deviations. As manufacturing quality requirements became more stringent, specialized inspection tools such as microscopes, gauges, cameras, coordinate measuring machines, and non-destructive testing equipment were introduced. Fixed machine vision systems later enabled automated inspection within controlled environments. However, many inspection tasks still occur across large facilities, distributed infrastructure, dynamic environments, and difficult-to-access locations where fixed automation is impractical. Mobile manipulators address these limitations by bringing inspection capabilities directly to the target assets.</p> <p>The combination of mobility and manipulation creates unique inspection opportunities. Unlike stationary inspection systems, mobile manipulators can travel throughout facilities, approach inspection targets from multiple angles, position sensors precisely, interact physically with equipment, and perform complex measurement procedures. This flexibility allows a single robotic platform to inspect diverse assets across multiple locations while adapting to changing operational requirements.</p> <p>Inspection workflows typically begin with the identification of inspection objectives. Objectives may include quality verification, defect detection, condition monitoring, preventive maintenance, regulatory compliance assessment, safety validation, inventory auditing, process verification, or infrastructure assessment. These objectives determine the types of sensors, data collection methods, analysis techniques, and reporting mechanisms required. Mobile manipulators can support a broad range of inspection objectives through modular hardware architectures and software-configurable inspection procedures.</p> <p>Manufacturing quality inspection represents one of the most mature application areas. Modern production environments demand increasingly high levels of precision and consistency. Products must meet strict dimensional tolerances, surface quality standards, assembly requirements, and functional specifications. Mobile manipulators equipped with cameras, laser scanners, structured-light systems, and measurement devices can inspect components throughout production processes. By identifying defects early, manufacturers reduce scrap rates, improve product quality, and minimize costly downstream failures.</p> <p>Visual inspection is perhaps the most common inspection method. Cameras capture images of products, equipment, or infrastructure, while computer vision algorithms analyze the collected data. Traditional machine vision systems relied on rule-based image processing techniques. Modern inspection platforms increasingly utilize deep learning and artificial intelligence to recognize complex patterns, identify subtle defects, and adapt to varying environmental conditions. AI-based visual inspection systems often achieve performance levels comparable to or exceeding those of human inspectors while maintaining consistent operation over extended periods.</p> <p>Surface defect detection is a particularly important inspection task. Manufacturing defects such as scratches, cracks, dents, discoloration, contamination, deformation, misalignment, and incomplete assembly can significantly affect product quality. Mobile manipulators can position imaging systems at optimal viewing angles and collect high-resolution data for analysis. Deep learning models trained on defect datasets enable automated identification and classification of abnormalities across diverse product categories.</p> <p>Dimensional inspection is another critical application. Mobile manipulators equipped with three-dimensional scanners, laser measurement systems, structured-light sensors, and metrology equipment can perform dimensional analysis directly within production environments. These capabilities reduce dependence on dedicated inspection stations while supporting real-time quality control processes.</p> <p>Inspection is equally important in machine condition monitoring. Mobile manipulators enable more frequent and data-driven condition assessments by autonomously visiting equipment and collecting sensor data. This capability supports predictive maintenance strategies that reduce unplanned downtime and extend equipment life.</p> <p>Thermal inspection has become increasingly important across industrial sectors. Mobile manipulators equipped with thermal imaging cameras can identify temperature anomalies that are invisible to the human eye. Many mechanical problems generate characteristic sound signatures before visible failures occur. Microphones and acoustic sensors allow mobile manipulators to detect abnormal noises associated with bearing failures, motor degradation, leaks, cavitation, or structural defects. Artificial intelligence can analyze acoustic patterns and identify potential issues long before catastrophic failures develop.</p> <p>Vibration monitoring is widely used for predictive maintenance and equipment diagnostics. Rotating machinery such as motors, compressors, turbines, pumps, and conveyors generate vibration patterns that reflect operational conditions. Mobile manipulators equipped with vibration sensors can collect measurements from multiple machines and compare observed data against baseline conditions. Deviations often provide early indicators of developing mechanical problems.</p> <p>Non-destructive testing represents a highly valuable inspection domain. Non-destructive testing methods evaluate material integrity without causing damage to the inspected object. Technologies such as ultrasonic testing, eddy current testing, radiographic inspection, laser profiling, and magnetic particle inspection can be integrated into mobile manipulation platforms. These capabilities enable autonomous inspection of critical infrastructure, industrial equipment, aerospace components, pipelines, and structural systems.</p> <p>Warehouse inspection presents unique operational requirements. This capability improves inventory visibility and reduces operational errors.</p> <p>Order verification inspection is increasingly important within fulfillment operations. Future healthcare robots may perform logistics, patient assistance, rehabilitation support, medication management, monitoring, diagnostics assistance, and even certain clinical procedures. Rather than replacing healthcare professionals, these systems will augment human capabilities and improve care quality.</p> <p>Home robotics represents perhaps the most visible future use case for the general public. While today\'s household robots are largely limited to cleaning applications, future mobile manipulators may become multifunctional home assistants. They could prepare meals, organize household items, perform cleaning tasks, assist elderly residents, support individuals with disabilities, manage deliveries, monitor home conditions, and interact naturally with family members. The realization of practical home robotics will depend heavily on advances in embodied intelligence and safe human-robot interaction.</p> <p>Elderly care will likely become a defining application domain. Global demographic trends indicate that populations in many countries are aging rapidly. Future mobile manipulators may help older adults maintain independence by assisting with daily activities, medication management, mobility support, communication, emergency response, and social interaction. These capabilities could significantly improve quality of life while addressing caregiver shortages.</p> <p>Personal robotics may eventually evolve into a new consumer technology category. Just as smartphones transformed access to information, personal robots could transform access to physical assistance. Individuals may own robotic assistants capable of supporting work, education, entertainment, health management, travel, and household operations. Such systems would integrate physical capabilities with advanced AI reasoning and personalized learning.</p> <p>Education represents another emerging opportunity. Future educational robots may serve as laboratory assistants, tutors, research aides, and collaborative learning partners. Mobile manipulators could support hands-on learning activities, facilitate scientific experimentation, manage educational resources, and provide personalized instruction. Their ability to interact physically with educational materials creates unique opportunities for experiential learning.</p> <p>Scientific research environments will increasingly utilize robotic assistants. Laboratories often require repetitive procedures, sample handling, equipment operation, environmental monitoring, and data collection. Mobile manipulators equipped with advanced sensing and manipulation capabilities could conduct experiments, manage laboratory workflows, and support researchers. Autonomous scientific discovery systems may eventually combine robotic experimentation with AI-driven hypothesis generation.</p> <p>Disaster response and emergency management represent critically important future use cases. Natural disasters, industrial accidents, hazardous material incidents, and emergency situations often expose human responders to significant risks. Future mobile manipulators will assess damage, locate victims, transport supplies, remove debris, perform inspections, and support rescue operations. Autonomous coordination among ground robots, aerial systems, and communication networks could dramatically improve response effectiveness.</p> <p>Military and defense applications are expected to expand as autonomous technologies mature. Future systems may perform logistics support, reconnaissance, infrastructure maintenance, equipment servicing, casualty evacuation, and hazardous operations. Human supervision and ethical governance will remain essential, but robotic systems can reduce risk exposure while improving operational capabilities.</p> <p>Urban environments are likely to become increasingly automated through robotic infrastructure. Smart cities may deploy fleets of mobile manipulators responsible for maintenance, cleaning, inspection, delivery services, environmental monitoring, public assistance, and infrastructure management. These systems will interact with intelligent transportation networks, digital twins, and urban management platforms to improve city operations.</p> <p>Autonomous retail and commerce environments may emerge as a major application category. Mobile manipulators could support inventory management, shelf replenishment, order fulfillment, customer assistance, facility maintenance, and logistics coordination. Future stores may operate with minimal human staffing while maintaining high levels of customer service and operational efficiency.</p> <p>The growth of cloud robotics will significantly expand future use cases. Robots will no longer operate as isolated machines but as participants in globally connected intelligence networks. Knowledge acquired by one robot can be shared instantly across thousands of robots worldwide. This collective learning capability will accelerate performance improvements and reduce deployment costs.</p> <p>Digital twins will become deeply integrated into robotic operations. Every robot, facility, asset, and operational process may have a corresponding virtual representation. Mobile manipulators will continuously update digital twins through sensor data while using simulations to evaluate actions before executing them in the real world. This integration will improve safety, efficiency, and decision quality.</p> <p>Human-robot collaboration will become increasingly sophisticated. Rather than simply working alongside humans, future mobile manipulators will understand human intentions, predict needs, communicate naturally, and adapt their behavior to support collaborative objectives. Advances in natural language understanding, gesture interpretation, emotion recognition, and contextual reasoning will enable more seamless cooperation.</p> <p>Vision-Language-Action systems represent a particularly important technological enabler. These architectures integrate perception, reasoning, language understanding, and physical action within unified models. Future robots may learn new tasks from verbal instructions, demonstrations, videos, or written descriptions rather than traditional programming methods. This capability will dramatically reduce deployment complexity and expand accessibility.</p> <p>Multi-agent robotic ecosystems will likely become commonplace. Instead of individual robots performing isolated tasks, groups of mobile manipulators, drones, autonomous vehicles, and software agents will coordinate activities across entire organizations. Shared objectives, distributed decision-making, and collaborative task execution will create highly adaptive operational environments.</p> <p>Sustainability will also drive future use cases. Mobile manipulators can optimize energy consumption, reduce waste, improve resource utilization, support recycling processes, monitor environmental conditions, and enable circular economy initiatives. As sustainability becomes a strategic priority across industries, robotics will play an increasingly important role in achieving environmental objectives.</p> <p>The ultimate future use case may be the emergence of general-purpose embodied AI systems capable of operating across virtually any physical environment. Such systems would combine reasoning, perception, manipulation, learning, mobility, communication, and adaptation within a unified intelligence framework. Rather than being designed for specific applications, they would learn and perform tasks according to human goals and environmental requirements.</p> <p>In conclusion, the future use cases of mobile manipulators extend far beyond the applications currently deployed today. Advances in embodied intelligence, artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, cloud robotics, digital twins, and human-robot interaction are transforming mobile manipulators into versatile physical intelligence platforms. These systems will influence manufacturing, healthcare, construction, infrastructure, agriculture, energy, education, research, disaster response, smart cities, and domestic life. As robotic capabilities continue to evolve, mobile manipulators are expected to become one of the most important enabling technologies of the twenty-first century, fundamentally reshaping how humans interact with the physical world and how work is performed across nearly every sector of society.</p> <p>Author: Richard Minsoo Go LinkedIn: Richard Minsoo Go</p> <p>DEV Community — A space to discuss and keep up software development and manage your software career</p> <p>Built on Forem — the open source software that powers DEV and other inclusive communities.</p> <p>Made with love and Ruby on Rails. DEV Community © 2016 - 2026.</p> <p>We're a place where coders share, stay up-to-date and grow their careers.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://dev.to/richard_minsoogo/mobile-manipulator-foundations-and-system-architecture-ch04-use-cases-en-5b4o" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9675"> <h2>#9675. Infinite Drive</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> A cloud drive you stream to give your laptop infinite space </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/infinite-drive?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1313305?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/infinite-drive" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9674"> <h2>#9674. I Put a 42-Desk Design Studio Inside My Coding Agent</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/nm8nG98qHqTz1QInSYwdBWsK07k1-4o83b5v.png" alt="I Put a 42-Desk Design Studio Inside My Coding Agent" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>I work on slow clicks and missing browser traces. I'm an OpenTelemetry Browser approver.</p> <p>I work on slow clicks and missing browser traces. I'm an OpenTelemetry Browser approver.</p> <p>I work on slow clicks and missing browser traces. I'm an OpenTelemetry Browser approver.</p> <p>In October, I pointed Desk Studio at its own launch card. Three roughs, one pick, three polish rounds, scored 8.4, then 8.5, then 8.9, signed off at 8.9 for $1.34 at list price. And I could see every one of those steps while it happened, which is the whole reason the tool exists.</p> <p>Before it, a follow-up like "make the headline bigger" would come back from my coding agent as a whole new design. New layout, new colors, sometimes new copy. Was the headline fixed? Couldn't tell, cause everything else moved too.</p> <p>So Desk Studio splits the job up like a small studio. Rough options first, then one gets picked with notes, a cheaper desk polishes it, a script checks the real pixels, and a senior desk signs it off or sends it back. I still use it on my own projects.</p> <p>There are 42 desks. The Design Manager runs in your own session and hands out work. The other 41 run as subagents, things like a Typographer, an Art Director, a UI Designer, or an Email Designer. Each one is just a markdown brief in the repo, so if you want to know how the Art Director decides, you open agents/art-director.md and read it.</p> <p>They're grouped into three tiers, and each tier is on a model that suits what it does.</p> <p>It all runs locally. The desks reach models through whatever CLI you're already logged into, claude, codex or agy, or an API key if you'd rather. Apart from those model calls and a few web lookups from the research desks, nothing leaves your machine.</p> <p>In Claude Code it's a plugin. For Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Windsurf or OpenCode it's one line in the project:</p> <p>Then you just ask like you normally would:</p> <p>The files land in .desk/out/<job>/ with a short note on who did what, the scores and the cost.</p> <p>To pass, every axis needs 8 or more and the average needs 8.5. Fail-proof, and it goes back to the builder with the screenshot. A builder that misses the same note twice hands the file up to a senior, and a senior that misses twice gets one round with the Art Director. After the round cap, the job comes back marked under the bar, with a note on which axis fell short, so it won't quietly ship something that didn't pass.</p> <p>Here's a real terminal run of exactly that, on OpenAI models this time. Proof caught a type-scale problem in round 2, the builder fixed it, and round 3 still came back under the bar cause originality only got a 6. The last lines say what's missing.</p> <p>Splitting out the pick was deliberate. Once a direction is picked, every round after that is a fix to that one design, so a note like "type sizes, not layout" means the next round touches type sizes and nothing else. When every round is a fresh design, there's nothing steady to measure against, which was the whole problem in the first place.</p> <p>Proof has no model in it for a similar reason. Contrast against the real pixels, text spilling out of a box, a headline sitting in a platform's crop zone, a script checks all that the same way every time and it costs nothing. The models get to spend their judgment on the stuff a script can't see.</p> <p>This is the launch card for Desk Studio itself, retold from its job record.</p> <p>The UI Designer made three roughs: an editorial split, a type-only one, and a framed one. The Art Director went with rough 2, the type-only one, and wrote why: "headline reads first at both sizes, only amber is the small lamp, fixes are type sizes not layout."</p> <p>You can overrule that. Every rough has a Pick this button, and if you use it, the pick goes on record as yours instead of the Art Director's.</p> <p>After that, the builder polished, proof ran every round, and the Creative Director scored each one.</p> <p>originality 7, under the bar, back to polish</p> <p>Round 3 got a 9 on seven axes and an 8 on originality, so 8.9 on average. This is the file it signed off.</p> <p>The whole job came to $1.34 at list price.</p> <p>About 60% of that went to judgment and 40% to making, and the three polish rounds together were ten cents. That's what the tiers are for. If you're on a subscription, it's a list-price estimate of usage, not an extra bill.</p> <p>Before the Creative Director ever sees a file, proof renders it in Chrome at each target size and checks:</p> <p>You can also run proof on its own against any HTML file:</p> <p>1.1 rebuilt the dashboard into the floor you can leave open while a job runs. It only listens on 127.0.0.1 , and the URL carries a token.</p> <p>The strip at the top is the job. In this capture of the launch card, it's sitting on round 2's sign-off; round 1 came in at 8.4, $0.77 is spent so far, and it's 17m 25s in.</p> <p>Pause at next step holds the job before the next step, and Stop job ends it there. Neither one cuts a desk off halfway.</p> <p>Below that is the floor, with a room per tier and a Proof booth. Each desk is a little bot that wakes up while that desk is working and goes back to sleep after. A ×3 on a desk means three of them are running at once, which is what you see during the roughs. Every room's sign shows its model, and Change swaps the whole tier.</p> <p>Clicking a desk opens its panel. The UI Designer's panel here says it's on anthropic/haiku and has done 4 runs on this job, 887k tokens, $0.45. You can switch just that desk to another model, for this job or as the default, or leave it a note that goes into its next prompt.</p> <p>On the right is who's working right now, and under it the studio log in plain words. One line from this job reads "Creative Director scored round 1: 8.4, under the bar", and the polish for round 2 starts on the very next line.</p> <p>The roles and cost panel is where the tiers make sense. The builders went through 2.9 million tokens on this job, and that still came to ten cents. The slowest single run was the Creative Director's round 2 sign-off at 11 minutes 25 seconds, which tells you where the time actually goes.</p> <p>Since 1.0.2, a job's event log also exports as an OpenTelemetry trace, with role timings, tokens and cost, so a design job can sit in the same tracing tool as the rest of your stuff.</p> <p>The repo keeps a gallery of 17 signed-off pieces with their renders, scores and costs. Most are for four made-up brands, one's for a real site whose brand the studio found in the project, and three are for Desk Studio itself.</p> <p>The scores come from the studio's own model reviewers. They're useful for comparing rounds of one job, not as a benchmark against anything else. The standalone runner only takes design for social cards right now, and the rest of the commands are Claude Code skills. The briefs install into other agents fine, though not every command works the same way there yet.</p> <p>Free, MIT licensed, and it runs on the CLI login or API key you already have.</p> <p>Then ask your agent for a launch card and keep the floor open. The code, docs, and full gallery are on GitHub, and there's a 50-second film on deskstudio.ai.</p> <p>What I use most is the rounds view. I pull up round 1 next to round 3 and check if the thing I asked for is the thing that changed.</p> <p>I Marked My Hero Image fetchpriority="high" - The Browser Still Asked for It 1.5 Seconds Late</p> <p>I work on slow clicks and missing browser traces. I'm an OpenTelemetry Browser approver.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://hackernoon.com/i-put-a-42-desk-design-studio-inside-my-coding-agent?source=rss" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9673"> <h2>#9673. 13 gluten-free dessert recipes : There's something for everyone.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2025-05/Gluten-Free-Brownies-6.jpg" alt="13 gluten-free dessert recipes : There's something for everyone." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The lack of flour in this recipe creates a velvety, fudgy cake that also happens to be gluten-free. Swooshed with a glossy chocolate ganache on top, this cake is a chocolate lover’s dream.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Callebaut Semisweet Chocolate Chips</p> <p>To make this classic fall dessert gluten-free, you just need to use gluten-free flour in both the pie crust and as a thickener. It can be difficult to achieve a flaky crust without conventional flour, but we’ve dialed in the perfect ratio of gluten-free flour to butter. Everything else you know and love about the dessert stays the same: a buttery crust and sweet, spiced apples.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Gluten-Free Measure for Measure Flour</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Almond Extract</p> <p>This crustless cheesecake is much more than the sum of its parts. Made with just cream cheese, sugar, salt, eggs, and heavy cream, it rewards you with a blistered, blackened exterior and a meltingly smooth interior. If you want to give it an autumnal spin, you can also make this pumpkin version.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Basque Cheesecake (Tarta de Queso)</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Half-Sheet Parchment Paper</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Triple Cocoa Blend</p> <p>If you're craving a classic treat or just need a reliable, easy dessert, this single-layer vanilla cake has you covered. It’s everything a weeknight bake should be: easy, quick, irresistibly moist, and full of flavor. Dress it up with chocolate ganache, macerated berries, or just a sprinkle of confectioners’ sugar.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Gluten-Free Vanilla Cake Pan Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Vanilla Extract</p> <p>Cheesecake may have a reputation for being fussy, but this recipe keeps things refreshingly simple. No springform pan, no water bath — just four basic ingredients for the filling: cream cheese, sugar, eggs, and vanilla. To make it gluten-free, just swap in gluten-free graham crackers for the press-in crust.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Pie Pan</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Triple Cocoa Blend</p> <p>The magic of this buttery, moist cake is two-fold: The almond flour-based batter is naturally gluten-free, and it comes together in just 10 minutes. As the cake bakes, the fresh berry topping sinks into the velvety, smooth crumb. No additional décor needed: The jewel-toned berries are all you need.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Almond Flour</p> <p>This golden Bundt cake is extra-moist and nicely tangy due to its fresh lemon juice glaze, while gluten-free flour ensures a soft, tender crumb.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Gluten-Free Lemon Bliss Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Almond Flour</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Chocolate Chips</p> <p>This cake is clearly a showstopper with its towering layers of tender cake, rich chocolate mousse, and fresh raspberries. This project bake will require some additional effort, but it’s well worth it for a special occasion.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Gluten-Free Chocolate Mousse Cake with Raspberries</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Round Cake Pan</p> <p>Brownies are the perfect candidate to go gluten-free. Since gluten usually adds chewiness and structure to baked goods, these brownies are even richer and fudgier without it.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you’ll need: Gluten-Free All-Purpose Flour</p> <p>Cover photo (Gluten-Free Brownies) and food styling by Liz Neily.</p> <p>Need to stock up on gluten-free baking ingredients? Check out our full collection of gluten-free flours, mixes, and dessert cups.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Recipes posts.</p> <p>Skip the store-bought stuff and bake gluten-free bread at home instead.</p> <p>For the fudgiest brownies, ditch the flour</p> <p>Everything you need to know to start making gluten-free sourdough.</p> <p>Gluten-free starter is possible! Here’s how.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/09/16/gluten-free-desserts" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9672"> <h2>#9672. Toki Matter</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> The Al agent that advances your matters </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/toki-ai?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1303858?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/toki-ai" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9670"> <h2>#9670. RevOps Is Quietly Becoming an Engineering Job</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://hackernoon.imgix.net/images/FrXwz2OOpLRbd0xvRNk08vBI1oo1-3483bcd.jpeg" alt="RevOps Is Quietly Becoming an Engineering Job" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p>Over the last two weeks, I've written here about a calendar table that knows November 1 has 25 hours, a customer health score that barely beats a coin flip, a 1961 warehouse formula that finds dead deals in a CRM, a Slack report that checks its own numbers before it posts, an exam for AI agents, a macOS job that died because of where it kept its log file, and why 3x pipeline coverage is a guess.</p> <p>My title is Head of Revenue Operations. Very little of that shows up in a RevOps job description.</p> <p>I started in supply chain, moved into revenue operations, and taught myself SQL along the way. For most of that time, the job looked the way people describe it: own the CRM, build the reports, run the forecast, keep sales and finance looking at the same numbers. That's still the job. But the way it gets done has changed, and I think it's changing faster than the job descriptions.</p> <p>The data moved into the warehouse. RevOps used to live inside the CRM and its report builder. Now the numbers that matter, from billing, product usage, payments, and the CRM itself, land in Snowflake or BigQuery. The person who reconciles them needs SQL, not a report wizard.</p> <p>Writing code got cheap. An AI coding agent will write the script that syncs the CRM, builds the workbook, or posts the report in minutes. That's the real shift. When code is cheap, more of RevOps becomes code, and someone has to run it.</p> <p>Running it is the part that didn't get cheaper. A script is easy. A script that runs at 7:45 every morning for two years, survives a laptop update, posts nothing when the data is wrong, and tells someone when it didn't run at all: that's operations engineering. And it's increasingly a RevOps problem, because the scripts are about revenue and nobody else owns them.</p> <p>If you work in RevOps, sales ops, or finance ops and you're wondering where to invest, here's my list, roughly in order of how often each one has saved me.</p> <p>SQL, properly. Not just SELECT and GROUP BY. Grain, joins that duplicate rows, window functions, time zones. Most wrong numbers I've chased came down to a join or a day boundary. (These six Snowflake patterns cover the ones I reach for every week.)</p> <p>One scheduler, and how it fails. cron, launchd, GitHub Actions, Airflow. Pick the one you'll actually use and learn what it does when things go wrong. Every scheduler has a way to fail silently. Know yours.</p> <p>Version control for anything that produces a number. If it ends up in front of a CFO, it goes in git. "Which version of the query made that slide?" should have an answer.</p> <p>Testing numbers, not just code. Reconciliations, check cells, golden questions with known answers. Code that runs is not code that's right.</p> <p>Staging and promotion. Somewhere to break things that isn't production, and a deliberate step between the two.</p> <p>Writing definitions down. Every metric needs a written definition that sales and finance have both agreed to. It's the least technical item on this list, and the one that prevents the most arguments.</p> <p>Working with AI agents. Give them a sandbox, an exam, and a short list of things they're never allowed to touch. Then let them do a lot of the typing.</p> <p>The risk in all of this is that RevOps turns into a shadow data engineering team: pipelines nobody else understands, a dozen scheduled jobs on one laptop, and a single person who knows how any of it works. That version is worse than not automating at all.</p> <p>So draw a line. Data engineering owns the platform: ingestion, the warehouse, the infrastructure everyone shares. RevOps owns the business logic and the last mile: the definitions, the reconciliations, the reports, and the small automations that move revenue numbers to the people who use them.</p> <p>And give the last mile an exit. When a RevOps automation becomes important enough that its failure would hurt the company, it graduates to the platform, with real monitoring, an owner on call, and a second person who understands it.</p> <p>Most RevOps postings still ask for CRM administration, reporting, and strong analytical skills. Those matter. But the people I see doing this job well now are also comfortable in a terminal, can read a stack trace without panic, and treat a scheduled job like a product with users.</p> <p>The title still says operations. More and more, the work says engineering. The people who do well will be the ones who take both words seriously.</p> <p>The pieces mentioned at the top, with runnable code, are on my HackerNoon profile.</p> <p>I'm Malek Damiri, head of revenue operations in Atlanta. I write about revenue operations and the systems behind it at malekdamiri.com.</p> <p>How to Generate, Recalculate, and Validate Excel Workbooks With Python</p> <p>Head of Revenue Operations. Revenue analytics, sales ops, and the SQL behind both. Atlanta.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://hackernoon.com/revops-is-quietly-becoming-an-engineering-job?source=rss" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9669"> <h2>#9669. Its sophisticated understanding of marketing psychology and brand voice, combined with its ability to generate compelling copy across multiple formats and industries, makes it invaluable for marketers and content creators who need to produce engaging, conversion-focused content at scale.</span></p><p><b><span style="font-family: Coda;">Key Features:</span></b></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Coda;">Advanced marketing copy generation</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Coda;">Multiple content type templates</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Coda;">Brand voice customization</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Coda;">Multilingual support</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Coda;">A/B testing variations</span></li></ul><p></p><p><b><span style="font-family: Coda;">Pricing:</span></b></p><p></p><ul style="text-align: left;"><li><span style="font-family: Coda;">Free tier available</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Coda;">Pro: $49/month</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Coda;">Advanced: $249/month</span></li><li><span style="font-family: Coda;">Enterprise: Custom pricing</span></li></ul><p></p><p><span style="font-family: Coda;"><b>Perfect For: </b>Marketing teams, copywriters, and businesses needing high-converting marketing copy across multiple channels.</span></p><h2 style="text-align: left;"><span style="font-family: Coda;">Conclusion</span></h2><p><span style="font-family: Coda;">The AI tools listed here are revolutionizing the content creation landscape in 2025, making it easier than ever to produce high-quality, engaging, and impactful content. By integrating these tools into your workflow, you can save time, unleash your creativity, and achieve better results.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Coda;">AI doesn't replace creativity; it amplifies it. As a content creator, your unique voice and vision are irreplaceable. These tools serve as enablers, helping you focus on what you do best—creating. Explore, experiment, and innovate. The future of content creation is here, and it's brimming with possibilities.</span></p><p><span style="font-family: Coda;">Embrace these technologies, stay ahead of the curve, and watch your creative potential soar. This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2025-07/Tarte-Tartin_2025_Lifestyle_ALT_H_1236.jpg" alt="This fall, reach for this unlikely apple ingredient : Apple cider vinegar is a baker’s secret weapon." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>As fall baking season settles in, you're probably reaching for apples — and the many flavor-packed ingredients they produce. Applesauce cooks down into tangy apple butter to be cradled in a flaky galette, while a drop of boiled cider can deliver supercharged apple flavor to crumb cake. But the baking ingredient you may be overlooking may be something you associate more with salad dressings and wellness tonics: apple cider vinegar.</p> <p>This tangy, apple-y vinegar is a secret ingredient in some of our favorite fall recipes, including cookbook author Claire Saffitz’s Cinnamon-and-Sugar Apple Pie. While lemon juice is the standard acid used in most fruit pie fillings, Claire opts for apple cider vinegar here to complement the filling’s flavors. “It helps as a flavor enhancer, and I also like that it’s apple cider in an apple pie. It’s a nice symmetry,” she mentions.</p> <p>Similarly, apple cider vinegar is used in the cooking liquid alongside sugar and butter to caramelize apples in a Classic Apple Tarte Tatin. The benefit is twofold: Vinegar’s acidity helps cut the sweetness of the caramel, and it prevents the apples from getting too mushy, instead maintaining their fork-tender texture.</p> <p>Pastry chef and cookbook author Natasha Pickowicz often leans into the jolt vinegar can add, including adding a few drops to her cake soaks for an additional layer of flavor. “Cake soaks should have a balance of tart, sweet, and savory notes — just like vinaigrette for your favorite salad,” she writes in her cookbook More Than Cake. It can add intrigue to layered cakes like this Golden Spice Cake or Pumpkin Layer Cake. In her cookbook, she also calls for a glaze spiked with apple cider vinegar to brush onto an apple tart after baking. It’s the finishing touch “to further emphasize the tart’s resolute apple-ness,” she writes.</p> <p>Apple cider vinegar doesn’t need to be limited to only apple desserts, either. In our Old-Fashioned Pecan Pie, we call for apple cider vinegar as a foil to the brown sugar filling’s cloying sweetness. A spoonful of apple cider vinegar may not announce itself boldly, but it makes a small splash for brighter, more balanced bakes.</p> <p>For more fall baking inspiration, check out our Fall Flavor Edit.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>A grocery store shortcut for bakery-worthy treats.</p> <p>It's got cinnamon-scented apples, rich vanilla cake, and a sheer sweet glaze.</p> <p>Eschew classic crust and enter a diverse world of beloved fruit desserts.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/09/24/apple-cider-vinegar-recipes" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9666"> <h2>#9666.
