</script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9625"> <h2>#9625. 16 pumpkin recipes, from cakes and cookies to bars and bread: We've got a marbled pumpkin cake, chewy pumpkin cookies, and even pumpkin milk bread.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/Pumpkin-Snickerdoodle-Cookies_FALL-26_BOTW_2026_Action_H_0693.jpg" alt="16 pumpkin recipes, from cakes and cookies to bars and bread: We've got a marbled pumpkin cake, chewy pumpkin cookies, and even pumpkin milk bread." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>It’s that time of year when pumpkin spice everything starts appearing on store shelves — candles, lip balm, air fresheners, beer, and of course, the ubiquitous PSL (pumpkin spice latte). That means fall is here, and more importantly, that pumpkin should make a grand return to your kitchen! Pull out your canned pumpkin — or better yet, make your own pumpkin purée — and stock your pantry with pumpkin pie spice, because we have the best pumpkin recipes to bake this fall.</p> <p>This Pumpkin Swirl Cake takes my breath away every time I unmold it from its intricate loaf pan. The anticipation keeps building until I slice into the pound cake-like loaf and reveal the swirled pattern inside, marbled with both vanilla and spiced pumpkin batter. (Don’t fret if you don’t have the specialty loaf pan — this can also be baked in a standard loaf pan and adorned with a simple confectioners’ sugar icing.)</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Patch O Pumpkins Loaf Pan and Pure Vanilla Plus</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice and Sparkling Sugar</p> <p>A cousin of Belgian-style Liège waffles, these Pumpkin Sugar Crunch Waffles have caramelized edges and a pleasant chew that’s reminiscent of brioche. The yeasted batter has pumpkin in it for flavor and color, plus Swedish pearl sugar that melts into pockets of crispy sugar. The best part? The batter rests overnight, so if you prepare it the night ahead, all you have to do the next morning is scoop and cook the batter for hot, crispy waffles in just a few minutes.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Pumpkin Sugar Crunch Waffles</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Swedish Pearl Sugar</p> <p>I used to make the same pumpkin pie recipe for years, and it always left me wanting a little more excitement. Then I found this Smooth and Spicy Pumpkin Pie and never looked back! The generously spiced filling uses nutmeg, ginger, cloves, and Vietnamese cinnamon to create a more flavorful pie than traditional versions. The secret to its silky-smooth texture? Corn syrup, which is an invert sugar and keeps the custard from becoming grainy. Substitute another invert sugar like honey or maple syrup if you like; I use maple syrup.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Smooth and Spicy Pumpkin Pie</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Vietnamese Cinnamon, Ginger, and Nutmeg</p> <p>Whenever I have these tender, golden scones on hand, I look forward to getting out of bed the next morning because I know they’re waiting for me. They can be easily customized to use a range of mix-ins, depending on what you have in your pantry. My personal preference is a mix of crystallized ginger and Cinnamon Sweet Bits.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Harvest Pumpkin Scones (or Gluten-Free Pumpkin Scones)</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Mini Diced Ginger and Cinnamon Sweet Bits</p> <p>If you’re looking for a way to make your whole kitchen smell like fall, these one-bowl, easy pumpkin muffins deliver — and fast. They’re ready in under an hour, so you can spend less time measuring, mixing, and cleaning and more time tackling your autumn bucket list.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Standard Muffin Pan</p> <p>Making banana bread is an almost weekly activity in my house — except during fall, when we pivot to pumpkin bread instead. This is a quick, easy bake that satisfies my craving for something pumpkin-y, and it uses a simple trick to concentrate the pumpkin flavor and ensure the loaf is perfectly textured: The pumpkin purée is reduced on the stovetop to cook off excess moisture. (The process is similar to browning butter.) As a result, the final loaf is packed with pumpkin flavor.</p> <p>Get the recipe: The Most Pumpkin Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Bread</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Ginger and Semisweet Chocolate Chips</p> <p>These bars have all the cozy, spiced goodness of the classic dessert in a portable, crowd-friendly form. The buttery, brown sugar crust gets pressed into the pan (no rolling out pie dough!), and the silky pumpkin filling comes together with just a handful of ingredients. The (optional but highly recommended) sour cream whipped topping brings a slight tanginess and completes the traditional pumpkin pie experience.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice</p> <p>This Pumpkin Milk Bread is exceptionally soft, squishy, and feather-light, while also packing in a lot of pumpkin. Pumpkin can often weigh down baked goods, but here the combination of a tangzhong, bread flour, and a long mix makes this bread simultaneously moist and high-rising.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Instant Yeast</p> <p>This tender pumpkin crumb cake is for people who double the chocolate chips in pumpkin bread and the streusel on coffee cake. Atop the thin layer of spiced pumpkin cake lays a heavy blanket of buttery crumbs with a bold chocolate flavor, thanks to Dutch-processed cocoa powder.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Chocolate-Pumpkin Crumb Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Black Cocoa</p> <p>These Pumpkin Cupcakes, with their piped swirl of cream cheese frosting, are the ideal way to celebrate fall birthdays. The cupcakes are super tender, thanks to the addition of cake flour and oil. Sour cream and brown sugar add tanginess and molasses-y sweetness while also preventing the cupcakes from being dry.</p> <p>For more cupcake decorating ideas, see our YouTube video: Decorate Cupcakes Better Than Ever.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Cake Flour (or Gluten-Free Measure for Measure Flour)</p> <p>My husband’s favorite fall dessert is Pumpkin Whoopie Pies, hands down. He can’t resist these subtly sweet cakes sandwiching rich cream cheese filling. This recipe has a few extra bells and whistles to take it over the top: Bread and Cake Enhancer to keep the cakes extra soft and fresh, xanthan gum in the filling to give it a smooth mouthfeel, and diced crystallized ginger for a bit of extra zing in the filling.</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Bread and Cake Enhancer, Xanthan Gum, and Mini Diced Ginger</p> <p>The next time there’s a rainy weekend, I’m taking on a project bake: our Pumpkin Cream Cheese Danish. It’s a multiday process and laminating dough is a labor of love, but the final product is worth the effort: buttery, crisp pastries filled with pumpkin and sweet cream cheese.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Pumpkin Cream Cheese Danish</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Baker’s Special Dry Milk</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice</p> <p>This Pumpkin Layer Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting is a show-stopping dessert featuring spiced layers of cake, not-too-sweet cream cheese frosting, and a blanket of melted caramel poured over the top. Will it be slightly messy to serve? Yes. Will anyone mind? Absolutely not.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Pumpkin Layer Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Pumpkin Pie Spice and Offset Spatula</p> <p>The pumpkin spice recipe I’m most excited to bake this fall is a mash-up of greats: Part-coffee cake, part-Bundt cake, part-pumpkin bread, this Pumpkin Espresso Bundt Cake deserves a category all of its own. It has two layers of espresso swirl tucked within a moist, spiced cake. Make it in your favorite Bundt pan or serve it as a loaf if you’re more of simple-is-better person. Either way, it’s great for snacking all day long.</p> <p>Get the recipe: Pumpkin Espresso Bundt Cake</p> <p>To make this recipe, you'll need: Espresso Powder and Bundt Pan</p> <p>For more recipes that are ideal to bake as the seasons change, see our collection of Fall Favorites.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Recipes posts.</p> <p>It’s peak baking season — here’s what to make.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/05/pumpkin-recipes" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9624"> <h2>#9624. Expo Simulators</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Cloud simulators built for agents </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/expo?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1314456?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/expo" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9623"> <h2>#9623. Upgrade Your Cheeseburger With A Request McDonald's Workers Love</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/upgrade-your-cheeseburger-with-a-request-mcdonalds-workers-love/l-intro-1794345313.jpg" alt="Upgrade Your Cheeseburger With A Request McDonald's Workers Love" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>McDonald's is probably the most iconic fast food burger in the U.S., and it's been around a long time. And, sure, White Castle may actually deserve the title of the first fast food chain, but the classic McDonald's burger actually began its journey when Dick and Mac McDonald introduced the Speedee Service System back in 1948. Although the burgers at the Golden Arches aren't cooked to order these days, if you're a fan they're not only tasty but full of nostalgia. That said, you can go beyond the basic McDonald's cheeseburger with a simple request that comes recommended by McDonald's employees: Order your next McDonald's cheeseburger with grilled onions.</p> <p>When asked how to upgrade this classic menu item, Wayne Kuhl, Director of Culinary in the U.S. for McDonald's said, simply, "You're grilling the onions." And former McDonald's chef and "Top Chef" Season 22 winner, Tristen Epps-Long responded, "I love to caramelize onions on the flat top while the Quarter Pounder cooks." Putting grilled onions on your cheeseburger will add an extra kick of sweet and umami flavor and bring it to the next level as they melt into the sliced American cheese. You can use it as a simple add-on or take it in some other interesting directions.</p> <p>Grilled onions come standard on the Steak, Egg & Cheese breakfast sandwiches, so it shouldn't be too hard to get your onions grilled. According to McDonald's employees on Reddit, it appears that if you ask nicely, they'll be willing to make it happen for you, but it's not a guarantee. That said, if someone with the title "Director of Culinary" for the entire U.S.-based menu operation recommends it as a top choice, it should be possible to do just about anywhere, especially if there isn't a huge line of people waiting to order. If you're not a fan of a cheeseburger, some grilled onions can add a big boost to every burger on the menu. They can be great even on a simple plain hamburger to up the flavor profile to something that's downright gastronomic with more texture and more savory, charred, smokiness.</p> <p>If you want to go completely out of the box, you can order an In–N-Out Animal Style burger at McDonald's by adding grilled onions and some extra accoutrements. And, according to a YouTube poster, you can even make your McDonald's fries Animal Style with a side of grilled onions, a couple slices of cheese, and Mac sauce. While it may not be a guarantee that you can get your onions grilled, it appears that friendliness goes a long way when you make your request.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2312798/upgrade-cheeseburger-request-mcdonalds-workers-love/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9622"> <h2>#9622. COVID-19 and Moral Injury: a Mental Health Pandemic for Frontline Health Care Workers</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2022/01/Provider.Depression_G_1217318117-1-scaled-1.jpg" alt="COVID-19 and Moral Injury: a Mental Health Pandemic for Frontline Health Care Workers" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>More than 2 years ago, the alarm and first warnings of a global pandemic sounded. Now with over 830,000 deaths caused by COVID-19 in the US, there looms on the horizon a second underlying curve with equally serious long-term consequences: a mental health pandemic.</p> <p>The mental health fallout from the COVID-19 pandemic demands recognition, intervention, and mitigation strategies. Among the many at-risk populations are frontline health care workers who have been at the epicenter of the global pandemic, working long shifts with at times a tenuous safety net and limited support, and caring for COVID-19 patients with limited resources, mixed messaging, and uncertainty with regards to an end to the crisis. The psychological effects in some health care providers are akin to the moral trauma or moral injury that is recognized in combat veterans with posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD).</p> <p>Mental health professionals and other health care providers caring for frontline health care workers who present with insomnia, depression, anxiety, panic attacks, PTSD, and suicidal thoughts should recognize and validate their experiences and moral injury. Intervention strategies including health promotion, resilience training, and ongoing multilevel support will play an important role in flattening the moral injury curve.</p> <p>As a rule, the frontline health care workforce is considered capable, competent, resilient, professional, and persevering in the face of adversity. However, COVID-19 presented as an unprecedented crisis unlike any other unforeseen disaster, eliciting fear, uncertainty, and anxiety, coupled with grief and loss, both personally and professionally.1 As noted by Warren D. Taylor, MD, MHSc, and Jennifer Urbano Blackford, PhD1:</p> <p>The pandemic created anxiety and fear in health care providers, from physicians and nurses to allied health professionals and first-line responders. We fear for the safety of our families and patients. We grieve for those who have died. We feel guilt for not being able to save all our patients, for getting sick ourselves, and for abandoning our families. Many adopted the phrase, “we will get through this together but none of us will survive unscathed.”</p> <p>At the outset, the shortage of equipment and resources, changing practice guidelines, and unpredictability of the workload rendered health care workers with a sense of powerlessness and loss of control of the conditions under which they were able to deliver care. The emotional distress and social isolation from family and friends exacted an immeasurable toll on the physical health and emotional well-being of the workforce, setting the stage for the inevitable moral injury.2</p> <p>Moral injury is a term that has been applied to veterans of combat. Moral injury or moral distress as experienced by frontline health care providers occurs when health care providers are forced to make decisions that transgress their professional commitment to patient comfort and care, and forcibly shift their moral compass. They are not able to meet the physical, emotional, and end-of-life needs of patients.3</p> <p>Watson et al noted that moral injury in health care workers “can occur when someone engages in, fails to prevent, or witnesses acts that conflict with their values or beliefs.”4 Moral injuries may result from the following, according to Watson et al4:</p> <p>The consequences of such experiences may include feelings of rage, guilt, shame, and anger and moral injury is the “lasting psychological, spiritual, behavioral or social impact that may result from these experiences.”4 The number of acutely ill COVID-19 patients and high death rate coupled with lack of resources and at times rationing of limited resources such as personal protective equipment (PPE) and ventilators added to the dilemma that frontline health care workers faced.</p> <p>In a study of 448 Jordanian nurses during the COVID-19 pandemic, the majority of nurses (64%) reported experiencing acute stress disorder (ASD) and 41% reported significant psychological distress, with a predilection for younger nurses compared to older nurses.5 However, coping self-efficacy was a protective factor with the potential to mitigate the severity of psychological distress.5 An online survey of nonhealth care providers (N=976) found that individuals with previous trauma were at highest risk for increased symptoms of anxiety, depression, and PTSD related to COVID-19 compared with individuals with no previous history of trauma.6</p> <p>The long-term mental health consequences of moral injury for frontline health care workers have important implications for workforce survivability and durability; however, research on this topic is lacking. In one of the few published studies on moral injury among health care providers, investigators looked at the thematic content of experiences reported by nurses following incidents meeting the contextual definition of moral injury (ie, events with unintended consequences, potentially causing patient harm or putting patients at risk for serious injury). The investigators found nurses reported experiencing “guilt, shame, spiritual–existential crisis, and loss of trust.”7</p> <p>COVID-19 has presented difficult and untenable working conditions beyond the scope of the challenges frontline health care workers are prepared for professionally. Frontline health care workers have experienced conflict and distress over prioritizing patient care vs their own safety, protecting family members from infection, and the reality that the supplies, medications, and equipment needed to save a life were not always available or were being rationed. Because of high infectivity, morbidity, and mortality associated with the spread of the virus, frontline health care workers were often in the position to be the only person at the bedside at the end of life with patients who were separated from their families. This is not how families should experience the loss of a loved one.4</p> <p>There is a body of research regarding the long-term effects of moral injury among combat soldiers.3 It is reasonable to expect that feelings of guilt, shame, anger, and self-recrimination stemming from moral injury in these soldiers may be similar to feelings experienced by frontline health care workers during the COVID-19 pandemic and that their experiences increase the risk for acute stress reactions with long-term consequences including increased incidence of depression, anxiety, substance abuse, PTSD, and suicide.4,8 Behavior changes including intrusive memories, avoidance of situations that are reminders of prior events, self-isolation, and potential triggers of traumatic memories are common in individuals suffering from acute stress disorder or PTSD. Additional responses to stress, trauma, and moral injury include disturbed sleep, emotional changes such as numbing, desensitization, depersonalization, and a decreased capacity for empathy and compassion. For some individuals, the consequences of moral injury may be an opportunity for reflection and reprioritization of values and an existential inner process of reflecting on what is important in life.4</p> <p>Given the consequences of moral injury, it is important for mental health professionals and health care providers treating frontline health care providers to recognize and identify those experiences that have the potential for promoting resilience.9</p> <p>An analysis of data from 2,579 frontline health care workers in New York City early on in the pandemic showed that key factors predictive of psychological resilience were positive emotions, self-efficacy, purpose in life, strong social support, and not engaging in maladaptive coping strategies (eg, substance abuse).9 Psychological resilience was described by the authors as, “the capacity to adapt and thrive while facing adversity or challenging circumstances,” leading to the question of how can institutions promote psychological resilience in frontline health care workers?9</p> <p>Initiativespromoting psychological resilience are critical.10,11 Interventions identifying those at high risk for moral injury and in need of support in the form of psychological first-aid and psychotherapy have the potential of improving resilience. Kameno et al administered the short-form of the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale with 4 additional questions, 2 regarding sleep, 1 on appetite changes, and 1 on alcohol misuse, in health care workers during the pandemic.12 The researchers found that women and nurses had higher rates of affective symptoms compared to men and other medical staff, respectively. The researchers noted that early identification and psychotherapy may improve psychological resilience and reduce psychological distress in nurses at high risk for maladaptive coping.12</p> <p>The need for institutional support, leadership support, education, and training is equally important. Leadership and management are challenged to identify those practices that address the needs of their respective health care workers.10 Survey findings on the expectations and needs of health care workers (physicians, nurses, advanced practice clinicians, residents, and fellows; N=69) during the first week of the pandemic at a single hospital identified the following 5 requests of their organization: hear me, protect me, prepare me, support me, and care for me.13 Management and leadership have the opportunity to promote resilience and show visible support for the health care workforce with unique initiatives to help reduce and mitigate the long-term consequences of moral injury and acute stress response.</p> <p>Similar to triage protocols and models to meet emergent health care systems demands from unexpected disasters, there is a need for a multilayered mental health care response for frontline workers. Self-care and wellness initiatives have the potential to reduce the long-term consequences of moral injury. Ongoing support, skills training, psychoeducation, and wellness education regarding strategies to address and process the experiences of frontline health care workers are critical for healing the wounds of moral injury. Empathic sensitivity on the part of mental health providers and primary care providers is essential. Listening to “the story” and having the opportunity to process and reflect on the self-talk related to the experience of moral injury can lay the groundwork for healing.</p> <p>Self-care needs should include the opportunity to seek out and have available a support system of peers and colleagues. All too often the experience of shame, guilt, and self-condemnation are obstacles to seeking self-help and lead to self-isolation. If allowed to process and reflect on those experiences, health care workers may be provided an opportunity for experiential growth and a redefinition of priorities personally and professionally.</p> <p>Leaders in health care have the opportunity to create and foster a culture of open, nonjudgmental communication. In the face of unpredictable events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, natural disasters, and social and political unrest that impact health care delivery, strategies are available to promote mental health recovery and return to stability and wellness among frontline health care workers.</p> <p>Catherine R. Judd, MS, PA-C, CAQ-Psy, DFAAPA, is an assistant clinical professor in the Department of Physician Assistant Studies at the School of Health Professions, The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center, Dallas, Texas.</p> <p>1. GAtrends</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Spike alerts for your keywords in Telegram, Claude, ChatGPT </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/gatrends?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1314471?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/gatrends" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9620"> <h2>#9620. Ditch The Mayo: Give Pasta Salad A Calcium & Flavor Boost With One Ingredient</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/ditch-the-mayo-give-pasta-salad-a-calcium-flavor-boost-with-one-ingredient/l-intro-1794244254.jpg" alt="Ditch The Mayo: Give Pasta Salad A Calcium & Flavor Boost With One Ingredient" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Mayonnaise is the thick and creamy matrix that disperses all the other flavors in your pasta salad, coating the noodles and giving the dish a great texture when cold. But if you want more of that tangy, rich flavor, plus a decent boost of calcium, try blending feta with vinaigrette next time for a tasty result.</p> <p>Feta is a crumbly, tangy cheese with plenty of fat and salt, making it intensely flavorful but also creamy under the right circumstances. When you blend it with a premade vinaigrette, you create a beautifully bright condiment that pairs quite well with just about any type of pasta, from whole wheat to semolina. Unlike mayo, it combines the smooth decadence of dairy fat with fermented complexity and has a thinner texture that sinks into the nooks and crannies of different noodle shapes. While tasty, the ingredients still pair quite well with other pasta salad secret ingredients, from curry powder to various vegetables, so you won't need to switch up your recipe too much.</p> <p>Daily recommended calcium intake varies quite a bit based on age and other factors, but it starts at around 1,000 milligrams a day for most adults. Getting this much can be a challenge, but feta has about 270 milligrams per 60-gram serving, or about half a cup. Compared to the practically zero milligrams found in mayonnaise, this is an easy way to convert pasta salad into something not only more flavorful, but also more nutritionally complex.</p> <p>Pasta salad is a pretty flexible recipe, with no real standard ingredients outside of the carb in its name and a dressing. This means you don't have to choose between flavor and nutrition, and there are plenty of ingredients that can check both boxes quite easily.</p> <p>The false assumption everyone makes about milk is that it's the be-all and end-all of calcium-rich foods, but there are plenty of vegetables rich in the nutrient. A single cup of cooked spinach can add a whopping 240 milligrams of calcium and tastes fantastic with a feta-vinaigrette dressing. It's also quite an unobtrusive vegetable that has little effect on your dish's flavor profile, adding subtle grassy notes that make the end result more complex. If you want to bulk out the texture instead, a cup of cooked broccoli adds about 60 milligrams of calcium and creates a deliciously chewy texture when left a bit crunchy.</p> <p>Pasta salads are all about selecting the right pasta shape for your dressing. Since this vinaigrette is a bit runnier than mayo, you'll want to stick with varieties that are short and curly, creating enough surface area for it to cling to. While varieties made with traditional ingredients only have about 18 milligrams of calcium per 100 grams, whole grain pasta has 28 milligrams and a more rustic flavor. This can help balance out the acidity of the dressing, giving the dish a great mix of brightness and earthiness.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2311023/ditch-mayo-give-pasta-salad-calcium-flavor-boost-feta/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9619"> <h2>#9619. What are flour enzymes?: Understanding a common flour ingredient.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/flour%20enzymes%202.jpg" alt="What are flour enzymes?: Understanding a common flour ingredient." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>If you look closely at a bag of King Arthur flour, you may see an unfamiliar ingredient listed there: enzyme.</p> <p>We’re extremely thoughtful about every ingredient we use, across all King Arthur products and recipes. Our Food Philosophy guides every decision to ensure the quality of what we create, and that includes the enzymes in our flour.</p> <p>Here’s exactly what flour enzymes are and why they’re included in flour.</p> <p>Enzymes are found naturally in wheat, and thus are already present in flour. An enzyme is a protein produced by a living organism that acts as a catalyst to bring about a specific biochemical reaction.</p> <p>The amount of enzymes in flour can vary based on growing conditions from harvest to harvest and year to year, so we add natural enzymes to correct for any variance and make sure our flour bakes more consistently — in other words, to make your baking even better. Those enzymes make up a very small portion of the total flour: less than 1%.</p> <p>The enzyme we use in our flour is technically called fungal alpha-amylase. That’s a pretty technical name, so it is commonly labeled simply as “enzyme” on ingredient labels. “Alpha-amylase” is the actual enzyme, and “fungal” refers to the fact that the living organism that produces the enzyme is a fungus, not unlike yeast or a mushroom. Amylase may sound unfamiliar, but your body makes and uses it every day. When you eat, it begins breaking starch into smaller carbohydrates so you can draw on it for energy. Amylases added to flour perform a similar function.</p> <p>Note: Though fungi are technically living organisms, enzymes are considered vegan, as they are not animal based.</p> <p>Malted barley is an alternative source of enzymes that King Arthur has used in the past, but we found the efficacy can vary batch to batch. By swapping malted barley for straight enzymes, the flour produces more consistent results for our bakers.</p> <p>Another reason we made the switch? Enzymes require less water and energy to produce than malt barley. As a Certified B Corporation, we're committed to being good stewards of our planet, so pivoting to a responsibly sourced ingredient with a smaller environmental footprint makes sense.</p> <p>To put it simply, enzymes are added to flours to improve baking performance — they do not change the flour's nutritional value. More specifically, they help create the foods that feeds yeasts. The enzymes break down complex starches into simpler sugars; this, in turn, provides yeast with readily available fermentable sugar (food!), which enables yeast to work continuously and supports both fermentation and crust browning. This results in improved bread volume and crumb texture. Most other manufacturers of flour and yeasted mixes use enzymes for the very same reasons.</p> <p>Ultimately, enzymes are yet another way for us to provide you with the most consistent flour — which means even better baking.</p> <p>Cover photo and food styling by Liz Neily.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>A baker’s guide to our new T85 Baker's Reserve Bread Flour.</p> <p>A guide to baking with self-rising flour.</p> <p>The best baking starts with the best flour.</p> <p>It all comes down to gluten-forming protein content.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/15/flour-enzymes" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; Hoverine</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Rive animation templates you can drop into your app </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/hoverine?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1314493?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/hoverine" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9617"> <h2>#9617. Forget Salmon: This Fast-Cooking Fish Has Fewer Calories</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/forget-salmon-this-fast-cooking-fish-has-fewer-calories/l-intro-1794216240.jpg" alt="Forget Salmon: This Fast-Cooking Fish Has Fewer Calories" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Salmon's rich intensity also means it generally has more calories, which can mean different things based on someone's dietary needs. If you're conscious of this and still want something that cooks up quickly (and deliciously), try flounder, a leaner, lower-calorie option that never lacks flavor.</p> <p>Exact calorie amounts can vary quite a bit, especially when it comes to wild versus farmed salmon, but even the leanest ones usually sit between 130 and 200 calories per three-ounce serving. Flounder populations, however, have a more uniform lifestyle and consistently clock in at around 100 calories per three-ounce serving. That brown or gray layer of fat may help a salmon migrate and survive cold waters, but flounder are sedentary ambush predators that don't have nearly the same energy requirements. On your plate, this means a fillet of flounder is lean, clean-tasting, and quite mild compared to a richly marbled piece of salmon.</p> <p>Because flounder is often thinner and far less fatty than salmon, that also means it cooks exponentially quicker. While a skin-on fillet can widen your margin of error, it's still much easier to render your tender fish into a dense, rubbery mess. Your best bet is to treat it like a lean steak and use a hot and fast cooking method, letting a bit of carryover cooking finish the center rather than trying to reach the perfect temperature in a pan or on the grill.</p> <p>Flounder is delicate, light, and can easily lose its natural flavor if seasoned too heavily. While it's not exactly a beginner-friendly fish, the best ways to cook it are often straightforward and focus on timing and temperature, not technique. Hands-off methods that require little manipulation or rely on a sauce for flavor are usually ideal and keep your meat moist and tender.</p> <p>If you haven't tried making a meunière yet, it's a classic seafood dish you should try at least once. Made by combining browned butter, lemon, and parsley, it's just flavorful enough to elevate your flounder without overwhelming it. Just about any French butter sauce, from beurre blanc to béchamel, is great with flounder because it adds a bit of richness and is a great vehicle for other tasty seasonings. Plus, they're flavorful enough that you'll only have to pan-sear each side of your fish, reducing the chance that it'll fall apart or overcook.</p> <p>Flounder grows more delicate the more it's cooked, so preparation methods that rely on you only handling it when raw are also quite ideal. Baking is a precise method, and you only have to move the fish once to transfer it to a plate. On the other hand, flounder is fantastic when deep-fried, and the breading helps it hold its shape. You'll still want to use a large, slotted tool and a delicate hand when fishing it out, but all you need to do is batter and drop it into oil for a great result.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2310441/forget-salmon-fast-cooking-fish-fewer-calories-flounder/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9616"> <h2>#9616. 12 Fascinating Secrets To Building Deeper, Happier Friendships (P)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/friends-1-2.jpg" alt="12 Fascinating Secrets To Building Deeper, Happier Friendships (P)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The psychology of friendship reveals how time, similarity, connection and social support shape our closest relationships.</p> <p>Friendships shape our happiness, health and sense of belonging in ways we often take for granted.</p> <p>Psychological research reveals some surprising clues about how friendships begin, deepen and sometimes fade.</p> <p>From the time we spend together to the subtle signals that draw us towards certain people, friendship is more psychologically complex than it seems.</p> <p>Together, these 12 studies reveal some of the psychology behind how friendships form, thrive and shape our lives.</p> <p>• Read members-only and premium content • Access courses • Adverts removed • Cancel at any time • 14 day money-back guarantee for new members</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.spring.org.uk/2026/10/12-friends.php" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9615"> <h2>#9615. Willo</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> A companion you talk to while you play WoW </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/willo-2?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1311043?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/willo-2" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9613"> <h2>#9613. For More Flavorful Fried Eggs, Add A Teaspoon Of This Spicy Ingredient To The Pan</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/for-more-flavorful-fried-eggs-add-a-teaspoon-of-this-spicy-ingredient-to-the-pan/l-intro-1794295496.jpg" alt="For More Flavorful Fried Eggs, Add A Teaspoon Of This Spicy Ingredient To The Pan" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.</p> <p>Know the right fried egg cooking hacks, and your breakfast can easily take on a gourmet twist. For one such easy enhancement, try a hit of spice — just a teaspoon of harissa will effectively flavor eggs. Hailing from Tunisia, this smoky-savory condiment consists of chilies, garlic, and a wide assortment of spices (often cumin and coriander), all blended into a smooth dark-red consistency. It's a bold but not overwhelming blend of flavors that shines alongside eggs in a pan.</p> <p>For the greatest ease amidst bleary-eyed mornings, you can buy the spice online in the form of paste in a jar or tube. Don't confuse the condiment with powdered harissa seasoning, a dry blend with a similar flavor profile, but not the right composition for this application — though it might do very well mixed into scrambled eggs.</p> <p>Instead, you'll want a whole teaspoon of the paste itself. Heat up the pan, and throw it into a hot neutral oil, creating an aromatic red bath of chilis and spices. Follow this up by cracking in a fried egg or two, and sizzle up the lot in the fragrant oil. You'll get eggs with a dark red color and a warm dose of spice, making a dish with a lot of flavor yet not much fuss.</p> <p>Fried eggs make for a wondrously versatile food, fit as both a dish garnish and a meal in themselves. Upgraded with an ingredient like harissa, such versatile applications continue — only now with a bold hit of spice. You can integrate the seasoned eggs into a wide array of dishes.</p> <p>Start by taking inspiration from çilbir, a Turkish egg dish consisting of poached eggs, pepper-spiced butter, and yogurt. Consider serving the harissa fried eggs atop a thick and tangy dairy canvas, like Greek-style yogurt or salty labneh. Scooped up with bread or pita, it's a satisfying meal that doesn't require much effort. You can also make a quick and easy shakshuka-style fried egg by creating a base of tomato paste and harissa for your eggs to simmer in.</p> <p>Once lunch or dinner rolls around, add a little heft to the dish. Harissa-spiced eggs make for a great topping atop extra crunchy chickpeas or a creamy batch of white beans. A pork chop topped with a fried egg is a tried-and-true classic, and the harissa element will lend the construction an extra touch of spice. Not to mention, fried eggs belong atop sauteed greens, too; it's a terrific enhancement to a bowl of kale, for example. Harissa-spiced eggs deliver an aromatic punch, making them a culinary combo worth keeping in mind.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2311804/more-flavorful-fried-eggs-spicy-ingredient-pan-harissa/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9612"> <h2>#9612. </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9609"> <h2>#9609. 9 Best Budget Olive Oils, According To Home Cooks</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/9-best-budget-olive-oils-according-to-home-cooks/l-intro-1794317707.jpg" alt="9 Best Budget Olive Oils, According To Home Cooks" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Olive oil is a highly coveted ingredient due to its rich flavor, versatility, and numerous health benefits. While the price of some olive oils — such as the $50 per bottle olive oil Martha Stewart stands by — might have you convinced this golden liquid is too pricey for your wallet, the truth is that's simply not the case. Home cooks know this precious oil doesn't have to cost an arm and a leg. While they may hold no accolades or Michelin stars, household cooks carry a wealth of knowledge when it comes to which olive oils are best for daily use.</p> <p>There are plenty of sensational olive oils found at affordable prices, from the mild and mellow-tasting to robust EVOOs bursting with grassy and fruity notes. Whether you're on the hunt for single-sourced EVOO or cold-pressed olive oil, there are plenty of budget-friendly options out there that don't compromise on quality. From those ideal for cooking with to those that add the perfect burst of flavor to finish a dish, it's time to reveal the olive oils that have earned heaps of praise from average home cooks like you and me.</p> <p>Prices are as of the date of publication and may vary based on region.</p> <p>Any culinary enthusiast looking to buy extra virgin olive oil in bulk should consider Costco's house brand for a great value cooking oil. Kirkland offers an assortment of budget-friendly olive oils in two and three liter bottles, ensuring home cooks won't be running out of this precious liquid anytime soon.</p> <p>Kirkland's Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil is particularly prized by home cooks, with supporters calling its aroma elegant and its flavor distinctive and rich. Others describe it as balanced, smooth, and mild, making it ideal for those seeking a mellower cooking oil. Aspiring chefs love its light flavor and aroma, stating it's not only great for cooking, but for whipping up appetizers, like a classic bruschetta caprese. An olive oil with a pleasing color and thickness, many consider it a great choice for everyday uses given its affordable $10.50 per liter price tag.</p> <p>However, those looking for a heartier-flavored olive oil may be drawn to try Kirkland's Spanish Extra Virgin Olive Oil, which is equally praised. Those who prepare meals on the daily appreciate its more robust flavor along with the $9.50 per liter cost, making it the most cost-effective of all Kirkland's EVOO offerings. Home cooks find it to possess fruity notes with a pleasant bite. Many, in fact, prefer it over Costco's more expensive Italian EVOO.</p> <p>Trader Joe's stocks a 32-ounce bottle of Premium Extra Virgin Olive Oil for just $12.49 ($0.39 per ounce), offering up a great choice for those counting their pennies. Crafted from a blend of olives cultivated in Italy, Spain, Argentina, and Greece, this cold-pressed olive oil (a method of making olive oil that includes no heat or chemicals, which many believe creates an oil with more nutrients and health benefits) is one home cooks call great quality for the price. Supporters pronounce it to be wonderful for both cooking and finishing dishes, with one EVOO enthusiast calling it the best tasting offering on the market.</p> <p>Family chefs appreciate the noticeable aroma of this EVOO, finding it to have a nice finish with a good amount of pungency. Reviewers describe this reasonably priced olive oil as truly delicious, praising the way it cooks. Home cooks declare it to be extremely versatile, being a great choice whether you drizzle it, use it in a fryer, or wield it in a spray bottle. Fans of this budget-friendly oil also appreciate the handy attached spout, making for easy pouring from this hefty bottle.</p> <p>A bottle that always states where the olives are sourced, you know exactly what you're getting when you purchase this wallet-approved cooking oil. An olive oil that is surprisingly well priced for the amount, Trader Joe's Premium Extra Virgin Olive Oil is one that makes a good, multipurpose olive oil, perfect for the everyday.</p> <p>Are you drawn to premium olive oils, like Graza, but put off by the high price? Well Trader Joe's might have just the item for you. The internet is calling Trader Joe's Main Squeeze Extra Virgin Olive Oil a great dupe for the more expensive olive oil brand Graza. Equipped with an incredibly handy squeezable bottle, home cooks describe this olive oil as a great cooking olive oil with a nice, grassy flavor.</p> <p>Undoubtedly, part of this EVOO's appeal is the squeezable container it comes in, which makes it easier to control the amount of oil released. You'll find no messy olive oil running down the side of the bottle post-use or accidentally sloshing too much into the pan, thanks to its adjustable top. Upon purchasing Trader Joe's Main Squeeze Extra Virgin Olive Oil, one home cook notes that this enjoyable olive oil will have you convinced you need to be splashing it on everything, from pizza crusts to pasta and soups. But, the reusable container this EVOO comes in is not its only draw.</p> <p>This olive oil is cold-pressed, imported from the Mediterranean, and can be delightfully drizzled over everything, from roasted veggies to burrata. Available in a sizable 25.4-ounce bottle for $10.99, this Mediterranean EVOO clocks in at an affordable $0.43 per ounce. Compared to Graza's olive oils, which average around $21 for a similar product, this makes it an alluring buy indeed.</p> <p>Found in affordable two packs and three packs at Costco, Terra Delyssa continues to be a budget-conscious olive oil beloved by many home cooks. A single-source olive oil crafted from Tunisian olives, one fan describes Terra Delyssa Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil as smooth and herbaceous, never holding any bitter notes, making it perfect for pan-frying and salad dressings.</p> <p>Currently offered for $34.99 for a 3-pack of 25.5-ounce bottles at Costco, this EVOO comes out to an enticing $0.46 per ounce. Home cooks love it for three simple reasons: It comes in a glass bottle, boasts a single country origin, and it tastes good. Household cooks praise this high-quality olive oil for its unique and versatile quality, stating it elevates the flavor of any dish you add it to.</p> <p>The fact that it's non-GMO and USDA organic doesn't hurt either. Even more intriguing, the olives used in Terra Delyssa Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil are pesticide-free, harvested by hand, and cold-pressed within four hours of picking. The result is an olive oil abundant in antioxidants, low in acidity, and high in polyphenol content. People also love the traceable nature of this EVOO. A quick scan of the QR code on the label lets you trace the story of your olive oil from the orchard to the bottle.</p> <p>Anyone looking for a single-source olive oil that won't drain their bank account should check out Trader Giotto's Sicilian Selezione Olive Oil. A product we rated the highest in our ranking of Trader Joe's best olive oils, this EVOO is truly one that stands above the rest. Its flavor is exceptionally smooth, with delectable fruity notes and a pronounced peppery end note to round it out. Better yet, this golden elixir costs a meagre $10.99 per 16.9-ounce bottle, amounting to about $0.65 per ounce.</p> <p>A bottle that is astoundingly affordable for a single-source EVOO, this noteworthy olive oil is rendered from olives that are grown, picked, and pressed on Italy's island of Sicily. The final flavor? An olive oil that has a light, peppery finish that tingles the throat — a signature of high-quality extra virgin olive oil. This tingling sensation is due to oleocanthal, a compound that causes a slight burn in the back of the throat, and a sign that the olive oil is fresh and pure.</p> <p>An EVOO that Consumer Reports also rated as one of the best extra virgin olive oils at Trader Joe's, this is a great choice for those looking for a product that won't go bad before you have a chance to use it up. While you can certainly cook with this olive oil, home cooks find this to be an ideal choice for finishing dishes.</p> <p>Those looking for a premium olive oil at a wallet-friendly price will be drawn to Aldi's Specially Selected Sicilian Extra Virgin Olive Oil. Weighing in at $12.35 for a 16.9-ounce bottle ($0.73 per ounce), this Aldi exclusive might be higher priced than other Aldi options, but it's actually quite the steal given its high praise.</p> <p>An Aldi exclusive olive oil that has rightfully earned a place in your shopping cart, home cooks herald this olive oil for being single-sourced, with all ingredients originating in Italy. Other culinary enthusiasts applaud this EVOO for its striking hue and hearty flavor, labeling the taste as subtly grassy. Many appreciate the dark glass bottle as well — a characteristic that helps protect this precious liquid from light, which can quicken spoilage and cause the oil to lose its robust flavor. If that isn't enough, this esteemed EVOO also bears a seal from Val Di Mazara P.D.O., signifying the specific region it comes from, in addition to approval from the North American Olive Oil Association, denoting its superior caliber.</p> <p>This Italian olive oil is one home cooks declare to be perfect for drizzling over just about everything from salad to pizza, as well as making a delicious olive oil cake. No wonder it took the number one spot in our ranking of Aldi olive oils.</p> <p>California Olive Ranch is a fan favorite among many home cooks.A brand that provides a range of products, from single-source 100% California olive oil to global blends, you'll find an olive oil to fit every price range here. Chefs eagerly praise California Olive Ranch EVOO for its standout flavor, declaring it to be great for a number of uses, from cooking and dipping to marinades and rubs.</p> <p>This cost-effective EVOO is priced at an inviting $13 to $17 for a 16.9-ounce bottle of the global blends, which are offered in mild, medium, and robust varieties. It's an olive oil home cooks find to be surprisingly affordable compared to other better-known brands. The medium global blend in particular strikes a crowd-pleasing middle ground, securing the perfect balance between peppery and mild while still holding a classic grassy characteristic.</p> <p>Still, if you're looking for more of a finishing oil, the 100% California might be more appealing. Devotees of this single-source, California-exclusive olive oil declare it to be well-rounded, mild-tasting, and incredibly delicious, making it a great choice for just about everything from marinades and sautéing to baking delectable desserts. Additionally, culinary enthusiasts love the dark, glass bottle this EVOO comes in, along with the non-GMO project verification and vegan certification. Priced around $18 to $20 for a 16.9-ounce bottle, it may be more expensive, but it's an olive oil home cooks claim to last a while.</p> <p>A preferred brand of chef Giada De Laurentiis, Lucini is a store-bought olive oil admired by many households for its flavor and versatility. Lucini Everyday Extra Virgin Olive Oil can be found at a reasonable $13.49 per 16.9-ounce bottle (about $0.80 per ounce), rendering it a pretty affordable option compared to higher end brands. One Amazon reviewer declared this EVOO to "be a steal" compared to what is being sold elsewhere in the U.S., calling the taste amazing and the price truly unbeatable.</p> <p>EVOO fans find the cost to be fitting for the quality, declaring you can definitely taste the caliber when dipping bread into this delightful EVOO. Just add a little salt and pepper, and this palatable olive oil will do the rest. One supporter preferred it over Lucini's premium olive oil, claiming the Lucini Everyday Extra Virgin Olive Oil to possess a stronger bite, with more peppery and complex notes.</p> <p>However, Lucini's Premium Select Extra Virgin Olive Oil has its backers as well. A single-source Italian oil, home cooks commend this cold-pressed EVOO for its smell, perfect for use in all applications, from cooking to salad dressings. They find the bottle perfectly sized, ensuring you use up the contents before it loses its quality. Priced at $23.99 for a 16.9-ounce bottle, it may be slightly pricier, but it's an olive oil well worth considering for its rich, buttery flavor and pungent finish.</p> <p>Many are shocked at the affordable price of BONO Sicilian Val Di Mazara PDO Organic Extra Virgin Olive Oil, given its similarity to higher-end brands in taste. With a flavor one Redditor described as "pleasantly bitter and grassy, with a rich mouthfeel," many are astounded by this EVOO's phenomenal flavor profile. One avid supporter named it the best olive oil they had ever tried, finding it devoid of any bitterness at all.</p> <p>Domestic cooks admire this non-GMO project verified, USDA organic certified EVOO, loving the gorgeous yellow color and authentic Italian flavors. Upon sampling, one olive oil enthusiast declared the taste to transport them back to Italy, conjuring images of dining upon mozzarella and fresh tomatoes drizzled with olive oil. Another supporter lauded the vibrant aroma and well-balanced flavor, professing it to contain the perfect ratio of peppery flavor and smoothness, which ends in a pleasantly buttery finish.</p> <p>While more expensive than other household brands, its $24.99 price tag for a 16.9-ounce bottle is pretty exceptional considering the Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) certified status of this single-source olive oil, which ensures the olives that make up this delectable liquid come solely from the Val Di Mazara region of Italy. The process is supervised from growth to harvest and processing, undergoing rigorous testing to confirm the quality before being granted a one-of-a-kind serial number, denoting its authenticity and lineage.</p> <p>To select the best budget olive oils recommended by home cooks, we assessed a number of online reviews, discussions, and social media posts by household cooks and amateur chefs. From here, we selected the most notable olive oils to be found at affordable prices, seeking out the best value oils that still held high-quality characteristics, such as cold-pressing, organic ingredients, or simply an exceptional taste. A range of olive oils were included in this article, from wallet-friendly options that are ideal for cooking and baking with to those that are best for raw uses and finishing dishes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2311069/best-budget-olive-oils-according-home-cooks/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9608"> <h2>#9608. The Traditional Kitchen Knife Bobby Flay Recommends Is On Amazon</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/the-traditional-kitchen-knife-bobby-flay-recommends-is-on-amazon/l-intro-1794307086.jpg" alt="The Traditional Kitchen Knife Bobby Flay Recommends Is On Amazon" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.</p> <p>Whether you're an amateur home cook or a seasoned chef, a high-quality chef's knife is one of the three knives you need in your kitchen arsenal. However, with so many options out there, choosing the right one can quickly become overwhelming. You'll want something versatile enough to finely chop vegetables, break down a chicken, and handle just about everything in between. Durability matters, too. A good knife should last for years, if not a lifetime, with the right care. And, of course, it needs to hold its sharp edge. Luckily, Food Network star Bobby Flay has a recommendation that takes some of the guesswork out of the process (per The Kitchn): the Shun Classic 8-inch Western Cook's Knife, available on Amazon.</p> <p>Before getting into the knife's many selling points, there's one thing we have to address. At $163.95 (which is the sale price — it's normally around $205), it's certainly not a budget-friendly buy. But there are plenty of reasons why we think it could be worth the investment. At its core, knife steel is a blend of iron and carbon, with manufacturers adding other elements to improve its performance. It's these added elements that set Shun knives apart from the rest.</p> <p>The Shun Classic 8-inch Western Cook's knife uses a proprietary blend called VG-MAX, which is specifically formulated to resist corrosion and wear while maintaining a sharp edge. It also has a high carbon content, helping the blade achieve the hardness needed for excellent edge retention. The combination of elements in VG-MAX gives the Shun an advantage over many more affordable knives made with lower-grade steel, which have the tendency to lose their sharpness far more quickly with regular use. In other words, you're paying for a knife that's designed to stay sharp, rather than one that needs constant maintenance to keep it performing.</p> <p>If the name didn't give it away already, Shun is a Japanese knife brand, and all its knives are handcrafted in Seki City, a region renowned for centuries of sword and knife making. Any kitchen nerd knows that Japanese knives are up there with German ones when it comes to quality, so just by looking at the place of origin, you can expect a considerable degree of craftsmanship to have gone into this blade.</p> <p>Interestingly, despite its Japanese origins, the Shun Classic 8-inch Western Cook's Knife doesn't adopt the traditional santoku shape, often considered Japan's answer to the Western chef's knife. Both blades are versatile, all-purpose kitchen knives, but they differ in their blade profiles and the way they're typically used. Neither is necessarily better than the other; that distinction largely comes down to personal preference and preferred cutting style.</p> <p>While the blade might not have a traditional Japanese shape, the handle certainly draws on Japanese craftsmanship. It's made from Pakkawood, an engineered composite created by stacking thin hardwood veneers and infusing them with phenolic resin, which is then bonded together using high heat. The result of this admittedly complicated process is a durable, moisture-resistant material that's less prone to warping and cracking than ordinary wood. This makes it easy to keep clean, although that doesn't mean you should put the knife in the dishwasher or leave it to soak in the sink. Even quality materials can't protect even the most durable blades from the harsh detergents, water, and high temperatures, which will inevitably cause rusting and damage over time. Hand-washing and drying your knife promptly remains the better option.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2311850/kitchen-knife-bobby-flay-recommends-amazon/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9605"> <h2>#9605.
