</script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9603"> <h2>#9603. Skip Regular Butter And Oil: Roasted Potatoes Are 10x Crispier With This Ingredient</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/skip-regular-butter-and-oil-roasted-potatoes-are-10x-crispier-with-this-ingredient/l-intro-1794238653.jpg" alt="Skip Regular Butter And Oil: Roasted Potatoes Are 10x Crispier With This Ingredient" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>A mistake everyone makes with crispy roasted potatoes is using the wrong cooking fat, which tends to burn under the high heat required for great texture. Regular butter and oil each have their strengths, but neither gets quite the same result as ghee, a type of clarified butter with Indian origins.</p> <p>High-smoke-point oil is great for roasted potatoes because it lets you use high heat to crisp the exteriors. However, it doesn't add much in the way of flavor, so you're missing out on an opportunity to layer on more depth. On the other hand, butter is great at making a hearty side dish, but the milk solids tend to burn at temperatures above 350 degrees Fahrenheit. Ghee, however, has virtually no milk solids and very little moisture, making it the perfect middle ground. With a smoke point of around 450 degrees Fahrenheit and a rich flavor, it's the perfect way to achieve great texture without sacrificing taste.</p> <p>The biggest difference between ghee and clarified butter is taste and color. The former comes "pre-toasted," giving it a deep golden hue and an intense nuttiness that essentially kick-starts the roasted flavor of your tubers. Even if you don't use the various tricks to increase surface area, your potatoes will taste like they have more crispy outsides than usual. A small amount helps them develop the perfect color, giving you a showstopping presentation that tastes great, looks amazing, and still lets you use your existing favorite recipe with only one ingredient substitution.</p> <p>Ghee's flavor is more pronounced than butter's or oil's, but it's still just as versatile. Rather than switching up seasoning, it's best to focus on how to increase the "roasted" factor of your potatoes. Increasing their surface area, ensuring they have as little surface moisture as possible, and using the correct type of pan are easy ways to improve their flavor.</p> <p>There's an easy British trick for roasted potatoes that makes them exponentially crispier: roughing up the exterior. By parboiling them, then shaking them in a colander, you transform the smooth outside into one covered in tiny little ridges and bumps. These have a far greater surface area, which means your ghee has more room to help brown the exteriors, so you end up with more crispiness than normal. Not only does this improve the flavor, but it also speeds up the roasting time since you aren't cooking a raw vegetable.</p> <p>Moisture is the enemy of crispiness and can prevent even ghee from creating a great texture. If you parboiled your potatoes, letting them steam-dry for a bit makes them easier to work with and removes excess water. If cooking them raw, it may help to pat the pieces dry first to remove excess surface moisture. Either way, a heavy-bottomed pan, preferably cast iron or stainless steel, holds more heat and can develop far better color and flavor than something that is thin, flimsy, or nonstick.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2310797/skip-butter-oil-roasted-potatoes-10x-crispier-ingredient-ghee/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9602"> <h2>#9602. Heavy cream vs. whipping cream: What's the difference?: Understanding the right cream for your baking.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/heavy%20cream%20vs%20whipped%20cream.jpg" alt="Heavy cream vs. whipping cream: What's the difference?: Understanding the right cream for your baking." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>If you’re baking a recipe that calls for heavy cream, or picking up a carton to turn into whipped cream to finish a dessert, you may be confused when you hit the dairy aisle. There’s “heavy cream” — but also “heavy whipping cream” or, in some cases, just “whipping cream.”</p> <p>So when it comes to heavy cream versus whipping cream, is there truly a difference?</p> <p>Aside from being delicious, there are very specific definitions and standards that must be met in order for something to be labeled as heavy cream. It is made by separating the fatty top layer from the base milk layer during processing. The FDA states that heavy cream is cream that contains no less than 36% milk fat.  Comparatively, milk has 0% to around 3% milk fat, as well as a higher water concentration. Because of its fat content, heavy cream retains a rich taste and, when whipped, it excels at creating stiff peaks that hold their shape for a long time.</p> <p>Whipping cream — sometimes called “heavy whipping cream” — is made using a similar process as heavy cream and is also the milk fat removed before milk is homogenized. However, whipping cream can contain somewhere between 30% and 35% milk fat content, according to FDA regulations. Because of its slightly lower fat content, it whips into a softer, more billowy cream, and it will deflate more quickly than whipped cream made with heavy cream.</p> <p>Luckily, the difference in taste and performance between the two types of cream are not very discernible. This means you can use them interchangeably in recipes — and it's okay if you accidentally buy the "wrong" one. Both can yield a delicious bowl of homemade whipped cream. (Can’t justify buying a whole carton of either one? We’ve got you covered with an easy homemade heavy cream substitute.)</p> <p>A note on King Arthur recipes: The King Arthur Test Kitchen prefers heavy cream in most instances, particularly when making whipped cream, because of the higher fat content. That said, you can substitute heavy whipping cream 1:1 in any King Arthur recipe that calls specifically for heavy cream without any issue.</p> <p>As a general rule of thumb, use heavy cream for making stable whipped cream for topping pies, layered desserts like tiramisu or banana pudding, and any sweet where the structural integrity hinges on the cream really holding its shape. Heavy cream can also be handy for making cream scones and drop biscuits, where the richness of the dairy can shine through. For more heavy cream baking inspiration, check out these 12 recipes that call on heavy cream.</p> <p>Cover photo by Danielle Sykes; food styling by Kaitlin Wayne.</p> <p>Justine Lee is a food writer, recipe developer, and culinary consultant based in New York City. In her free time, she is actively on a hunt for a good almond croissant.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>A fun party trick and a handy pie tip, all in one.</p> <p>A trip to your garden (or pantry) opens up a world of whipped cream options.</p> <p>The tip that'll give you portable, made-to-order whipped cream.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/19/heavy-cream-vs-whipping-cream" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9601"> <h2>#9601. Templify AI</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Powerful content editor for people who aren’t editors </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/templify?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1293281?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/templify" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9600"> <h2>#9600. Clinical Challenge: Cough, Fever, in Person Who Vapes</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2022/01/smokingvapingteenagerg51500842_1324038.jpg" alt="Clinical Challenge: Cough, Fever, in Person Who Vapes" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>A 16-year-old adolescent presents to the emergency department with a 3-day history of vomiting, tactile fevers, and a mild headache that went away 2 days earlier. The patient denies any abdominal or flank pain, dysuria, diarrhea, or other complaints. When specifically questioned, she acknowledges a slight cough but has no shortness of breath or chest pain.</p> <p>The patient’s vital signs are normal except for an elevated temperature (100.3 °F) and a pulse rate 133 beats per minute. Initial physical examination is otherwise normal with no rash, tonsillar exudate, rales, murmur, flank tenderness, or other abnormality. Chest radiographs (Figure 1-2) and blood work are ordered. Laboratory results are within normal range except for an elevated white blood cell count (19,000/μL). Pregnancy and COVID-19 PCR tests are negative.</p> <p>Can you diagnose this condition? What is the most important medical history question to ask?</p> <p>This article originally appeared on Clinical Advisor</p> <p>Psychiatry Advisor, a trusted source of medical news and feature content for healthcare providers, offers clinicians insight into the latest research to inform clinical practice and improve patient outcomes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/home/topics/addiction/tobacco-use-disorder/clinical-challenge-cough-fever-person-who-vapes/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9599"> <h2>#9599. Filament by Galaxy</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Move data using your terminal or agent. Fast & open source. </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/galaxy?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1282575?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/galaxy" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9598"> <h2>#9598. With Age One Aspect Of Memory Gets Fuzzier But Another Improves (M)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/smiling-senior-1.jpg" alt="With Age One Aspect Of Memory Gets Fuzzier But Another Improves (M)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Memory does not simply decline with age: some parts fade while others become stronger.</p> <p>Memory does not simply decline with age: some parts fade while others become stronger.</p> <p>• Read members-only articles • Adverts removed • Cancel at any time • 14 day money-back guarantee for new members</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.spring.org.uk/2026/10/memory-fuzzier.php" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9597"> <h2>#9597. 10 Protein-Packed Substitutes For Mayo In Chicken Salad</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/10-protein-packed-substitutes-for-mayo-in-chicken-salad/l-intro-1794335846.jpg" alt="10 Protein-Packed Substitutes For Mayo In Chicken Salad" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Chicken salad is like edible Americana, a comfort food that's beloved for its taste, nutrition, and versatility. You can find it in the prepared section of your local supermarket or on the menu of your favorite diner. Trying to cut down on carbohydrates? Have a scoop on a salad. Want a light and easy lunch? Have it as a club or between two pieces of toasted whole-grain bread. More importantly, though, chicken salad is like a ball of clay ready to be shaped by your taste preferences. You can take it in infinite directions: Mediterranean, Southwest, Spanish, French, Indian, Vietnamese. Have some extra sprigs of cilantro or half a bag of red grapes lying hanging around the fridge? Add 'em. Don't know what to do with those leftover pecans or knob of fresh ginger? You can throw those in, too.</p> <p>But the foundation of any respectable chicken salad is its creamy binder. In that regard, mayonnaise is the undisputed classic, turning your basic diced chicken breast into something moist, savory, and luscious. However, plenty of other ingredients deliver that signature smoothness — just with more protein. From tzatziki to silken tofu to labneh, there are tons of options that deliver both texture and an added pop of flavor. Whether you're minding your macros or just looking for a new spin on a classic dish, this list of protein-packed mayo substitutes is for you.</p> <p>Yogurt has a long and storied reputation as a health food, so long, in fact, that its beneficial properties are documented in Indian Ayurvedic medicinal writings from more than 7,000 years ago. Today, it's seen as a better-for-you breakfast option, loaded with beneficial probiotics, calcium, and, of course, protein. Yogurt, especially the more thoroughly strained Greek variety, has an excellent calorie-to-protein ratio (about 16 grams of protein per 150 calories when made with whole milk), which is why it has become so popular with bodybuilders and wellness influencers.</p> <p>However, Greek yogurt still has a place in ordinary kitchens, and it's especially useful for people looking for a healthier alternative to mayonnaise, cream cheese, or any other creamy, high-fat, high-cholesterol product, which is why it makes such a great addition to homemade chicken salad. Even when prepared with mayonnaise, chicken salad is a relatively nutritious lunch option, typically made with low-fat chicken breast, fresh herbs, diced veggies, and maybe some nuts or sliced grapes. Whole milk yogurt, which is creamier than low-fat options, builds on that by adding extra protein, moisture, and the richness synonymous with a good chicken salad. It also adds a little tang that complements the subdued nature of poultry and plays well with other common chicken-salad additions, like mustard, dill, or curry powder.</p> <p>It feels like every week there's another article or study being published identifying the benefits of gut health. This increased focus on the gut microbiome and the trillions of microorganisms that occupy it has brought all sorts of fermented dairy products, which are packed with probiotics and other useful bacteria, back into the nutritional spotlight. In this department, Greek yogurt is king (at least in the United States), but other styles are slowly making their way to the supermarket dairy aisle. One of them is skyr, also known as Icelandic yogurt.</p> <p>Technically classified as a cheese because its proteins are coagulated with rennet (a naturally occurring enzyme), skyr is dense, almost custard-like, with a mild sweetness and less assertive bite than Greek yogurt. Nutritionally, the two dairy products have an almost identical profile, although skyr is typically slightly higher in protein per serving due to a more rigorous straining process. But it's that straining — and subsequent thicker texture — that makes skyr such a terrific mayo substitute, delivering the same full creaminess without the more forward lactic tang of typical yogurt. How you use it in your chicken salad is a personal preference. If you like your chicken salad on the more unctuous side, use it as is; if you like it a little looser, thin your skyr with a tablespoon or two of milk, which may also help coat each ingredient more evenly.</p> <p>On a per-calorie basis, cottage cheese is hard to beat among high-protein foods, with (on average) 12-14 grams of protein per 100-calorie serving. Unlike yogurt, which is fermented with bacteria, cottage cheese is made through acidification. As milk becomes more acidic and the pH level drops, the proteins denature, clump, and coagulate into tiny little curds. Although the process is simple, there's a lot of variability between brands. Some are saltier or creamier or contain larger curds.</p> <p>But the most influential factor, especially regarding your chicken salad, is the fat content. While low-fat cottage cheese has fewer calories per serving, it lacks the richness needed to rehydrate dry chicken. Beyond extra unctuousness, full-fat cottage cheese adds salinity, clean milky notes, and a very mild cheese flavor. However, there's one major difference between cottage cheese and mayonnaise: Texture. Straight out of the plastic tub, cottage cheese can be, well, lumpy. This may not bother you in the slightest, but if it does, there's an easy workaround: Whipping the cottage cheese. You can do this with a hand mixer, mini food processor, or even just a big fork; the goal being to break those curds into a finer texture similar to ricotta. You can use the same technique to incorporate this high-protein food into smoothies, dips, and even macaroni and cheese.</p> <p>Hummus was the "it" food product of the early 2000s, but in the years since, it has faded in popularity. Maybe we were just given too much, too fast: Beet hummus, carrot hummus, lentil hummus, chocolate hummus — each variation obfuscating the beauty of this simple, timeless, life-sustaining food. Hummus, the type made from chickpeas, sesame paste (tahini), and olive oil, is an ancient form of plant-based protein foundational to Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines. When blended, the ingredients make a velvety emulsion that — depending on how much ice water or oil you use — can be spread or scooped over everything, from bulgur wheat to falafel wraps.</p> <p>It's also a great addition to salads — including ones made from chicken. Here, hummus provides an extra protein boost as well as some much-needed fattiness. Its blend of Middle Eastern spices — cumin, sumac, garlic, za'atar — contributes a warmth and brightness that cuts through the inherent blandness of cooked chicken breast. If using hummus as the foundation of your chicken salad, consider adding other Mediterranean ingredients, like capers, olives, walnuts, almonds, fresh tomato, or cucumbers. You can use your favorite supermarket brand, or just quickly whip up delicious hummus at home.</p> <p>Probably the most underrated ingredient on this list, silken tofu is a centuries-old, plant-based protein with limitless applications. Like other forms of bean curd, silken tofu is made from soybeans, but it's worlds different from soft, medium, or firm varieties. While it comes in similar packaging, silken tofu is hardly solid; it's more like a pudding or flan that will fall apart if you try to pick it up with a fork. However, it's precisely this loose creaminess that makes silken tofu such a terrific substitute for mayonnaise in your next chicken salad.</p> <p>Besides being a great protein source — containing around 20 grams per 16-ounce package — silken tofu can easily be made smooth and pourable. When blended, it becomes something akin to Alfredo sauce, with a velvety consistency that's ideal for coating chicken. Another advantage of silken tofu is its taste — or lack thereof. You're dealing with a blank canvas here, one that will quickly absorb whatever seasonings, herbs, or sauces you mix with it. It may need some doctoring to get the texture right, but just use this as another opportunity to add flavor. Try adding cilantro and lime, tarragon and sherry vinegar, or hot sauce, for a Buffalo wing-inspired chicken salad.</p> <p>There are only so many ways to add creaminess to food without relying on dairy, a fatty emulsion, or some complicated form of food chemistry. Adding a can of blended beans is one of them. Legumes, like black beans, kidney beans, and butter beans, have a starchy center that turns smooth and pillowy when blended. Most commercial varieties you find at your typical supermarket are good for cooking, but some have a more distinct flavor than others.</p> <p>When making chicken salad, it's best to use beans with a clean, neat taste and not too much earthiness. For this, white, cannellini, or Great Northern beans are best. They won't overwhelm the other ingredients in your chicken salad, but they also aren't entirely neutral-tasting, either. The key to using these legumes is to purée them with different spices, herbs, and condiments, like Worcestershire sauce, miso, or a splash of vinegar. To achieve a texture that's similar to mayonnaise, you'll likely need to add some liquid or fat. Olive or another neutral oil works, but adding a heavily seasoned broth will give you an even better result. To do this, make a quick pan sauce with sautéed aromatics, seasonings, and stock; add it to your beans, then blend everything in a blender or food processor.</p> <p>This one is a little sneaky. Egg yolks are inherently fatty, but they also contain natural emulsifiers that turn into a creamy paste when blended. That means you don't have to add a drop of mayonnaise (which, ironically, is made predominantly from egg yolks) to achieve a luscious texture. But egg salad brings more to the party than just creaminess. If you've ever watched a TikTok nutritionist worth their creatine, then you're probably frustratingly aware that egg whites are one of nature's purest protein sources.</p> <p>This combination of smooth, fatty yolk and protein-rich white makes egg salad an incredible substitute for mayo. It's a tongue-in-cheek pairing, for sure, but this whimsical culinary mashup also delivers on taste. Because eggs are a tad sulfurous on their own, season them generously with ingredients like Dijon mustard, capers, lemon juice, smoked paprika, or even a few shakes of curry powder. However, the key to achieving a natural creaminess is proper egg cookery, which essentially boils down to not overcooking your hard-boiled eggs. The answer: A quick dunk in the ice bath for about 10-15 minutes to halt cooking and preserve those fluffy yolks.</p> <p>Want the nutritional upside of yogurt with an added burst of refreshing Mediterranean flavors? Sounds like it's tzatziki time. The yogurt-based dip is most closely associated with Greek cuisine, serving as a cooling counterpoint to robustly seasoned grilled meats, fried zucchini, and platters of pita. And, while its protein content isn't on the same level as skyr or cottage cheese, it isn't negligible, either, which is why it's another smart mayo substitute for your next chicken salad.</p> <p>Tzatziki looks simple, but it delivers a chorus of complex flavors that few condiments can match. It's all things smooth, rich, tangy, and fresh, thanks to a blend of fresh herbs and other aromatics. Besides yogurt, the predominant ingredient is cucumber. Paired with fresh mint, dill, and garlic, this creates a clean, powerful taste profile. It instantly elevates ordinary chicken into something moist and tender. Slip your tzatziki-coated chicken salad into a pita and top with shredded lettuce, tomato, black olives, and sliced red onion for a memorable lunch. While tzatziki is popular, it can be difficult to find good options in your average supermarket. Thankfully, a quality tzatziki sauce is easy to put together; just remember to squeeze the moisture out of your cucumbers. Otherwise, your sauce will be too wet and separate.</p> <p>Labneh is made by straining Greek yogurt in cheesecloth until you remove the remaining liquid whey. This not only creates a denser product, but it also concentrates the flavor. It's traditionally made with goat's milk, which is a little grassy on the palate and has a slightly tangier finish than a cow's milk cheese or yogurt. Unlike yogurt, though, which you typically eat with a spoon, labneh is more of a dip, perfect for crudités, pita, lavash, or even grilled fruits. It has a decadent mouthfeel and is decidedly more savory, especially when dressed with olive oil, making it a nice way to rejuvenate an otherwise tired chicken salad.</p> <p>But there's no reason to pigeonhole this spreadable yogurt as savory or sweet; it works beautifully with both taste profiles. You can roll it in za'atar, sumac, and fresh mint, or crust it with pistachios and drizzle it with honey. Since it's the thickest yogurt-based product on this list, when using it for chicken salad, you'll likely want to add a splash of milk or a non-dairy alternative to loosen it up. If you can't find labneh in stores, you can literally just add Greek yogurt to a cheesecloth, hang it above your sink, and let it drip for a few hours until it's firm and extra creamy.</p> <p>Like most dairy products, feta is a solid protein source, with about 4 grams per 2-ounce serving; however, it differs from other cheeses because it's brined in a salt-water and whey solution rather than traditionally aged. This process helps preserve the cheese while also imbuing it with its signature salinity. If you've been lucky enough to try quality feta, you know that this soft, crumbly cheese packs a punch. In the mouth, it has a clean, fresh cream flavor and mild tang, making it a natural partner for grilled meats like beef, lamb, or chicken.</p> <p>Feta isn't spreadable, nor does it melt, but you can easily transform its texture by dropping a few chunks into a blender or food processor and "whipping" it until smooth. The result is smooth, salty, and spoonable — and perfect for chicken salad. When using whipped feta, consider both its salt content and mild acidic bite. These are strong flavors that should be balanced with other sweet and savory ingredients. Try pairing it with starchy, nutty, or mildly sweet foods like roasted butternut squash, pistachios, dried cranberries, or nectarines.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2312434/protein-packed-substitutes-mayo-in-chicken-salad/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9596"> <h2>#9596. How to clean cast iron  : It’s simpler than you think.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/How%20to%20Clean%20Cast%20Iron_Blog_2026_Shot%201_0070.jpg" alt="How to clean cast iron  : It’s simpler than you think." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Despite what you may have heard, cleaning and maintaining a cast iron skillet or Dutch oven isn’t difficult. It’s practically impossible to ruin a well-seasoned skillet, and despite your best efforts, sometimes food will stick. If your cast iron is covered in stuck-on bits of cheese from a batch of Crispy Cheesy Pan Pizza, here's how to clean it.</p> <p>We can settle the debate once and for all: Yes, you can use soap to clean your cast iron. Dishwashing soap will not damage the seasoning that makes your skillet non-stick. Polymerized oil creates the layer of seasoning through heat, and dish soap isn’t strong enough to break that bond.</p> <p>No, you cannot clean a cast iron skillet in the dishwasher. This will degrade the seasoning layer and cause it to rust.</p> <p>You should not soak a cast iron pan either; the water will cause it to rust. If you do end up rusting your pan, you can still rescue it by scrubbing off the rust then re-seasoning the pan.</p> <p>Using warm, soapy water, scrub the pan with a stiff-bristled brush or sponge to remove any food residue. Avoid harsh, abrasive scrubbers like steel wool or metal pads, which can strip the pan of its seasoning.</p> <p>Once cleaned, fully dry the pan with a kitchen towel, or place it onto a burner over low heat so the water fully evaporates. Don’t walk away from the pan — it can quickly get smoky once the water has evaporated.</p> <p>Regardless of which method you prefer, it’s imperative that the pan is fully dry. Water (not soap!) is the enemy of cast iron, which can cause it to rust. Once dry, add a few drops of neutral oil and spread all over the pan with a towel.</p> <p>Photography by Patrick Marinello; styling by Yekaterina Boytsova</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>Topping inspiration for your favorite pizza</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/21/how-to-clean-cast-iron" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9595"> <h2>#9595. Burnstate</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Claude Code, Codex & Cursor limits, paced in your menu bar </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/burnstate?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1311191?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/burnstate" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9594"> <h2>#9594. Google Pixel Tag</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Google’s $30 Android-ready tracking tag </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/google?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1312154?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/google" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9593"> <h2>#9593. Forget Apple Pie: An Easier Thanksgiving Dessert Bobby Flay Recommends</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/forget-apple-pie-an-easier-thanksgiving-dessert-bobby-flay-recommends/l-intro-1794506771.jpg" alt="Forget Apple Pie: An Easier Thanksgiving Dessert Bobby Flay Recommends" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>While turkey and stuffing may be the centerpieces on a Thanksgiving table during the main course, almost everyone knows that the meal isn't complete without a sweet finish. And no other type of dessert is more appropriate for this holiday than pie, including one filled with tender, sweet apples. While you can get top-ranking apple pies from a grocery store, making your own can feel much more satisfying and give you bragging rights. However, assembling one from scratch can be an ordeal. Luckily, chef Bobby Flay has a much easier solution: Make a crostata instead.</p> <p>A crostata is a type of Italian tart that is traditionally made with pasta frolla, a dough whose ingredients typically include flour, sugar, butter, and eggs, although recipes can differ. It's a versatile dessert that can have many different fillings, including one containing ricotta that's one of Rick Steves' favorite desserts in Italy. The form of a crostata is equally varied, as it can be made in a tart pan or free-form, and it's this latter style that Flay prefers.</p> <p>In an Instagram post, Flay shared, "My tarts, pies and cakes are going to have that 'rustic' look no matter what ... a [crostata] is supposed to feel that way so it's my go-to move!" And if you feel the same way, you should give this dessert a spin. The biggest advantage it has over a traditional pie is its simplicity. All you need to do is place the dough on a baking sheet, add your apples to the center, and fold up the crust over the edges of the filling to hold everything together. Your dough doesn't even need to be a perfect circle, and there's no need for a top crust.</p> <p>A crostata is simpler to make than many pies, but there's still a little bit of technique and preparation involved in assembling one. While pasta frolla is the traditional crust, you're not bound to using it, and even your favorite all-purpose pie crust recipe can work to bake a rustic apple crostata for Thanksgiving. You can also opt to use premade pie crust from the supermarket if making it from scratch is a little too time-consuming, especially if you have a litany of other dishes to prepare for the holiday. When assembling your crostata, you want to make sure that your crust remains cold but is still pliable.</p> <p>Now comes time for the filling. Since a crostata is a flatter riff on a pie, you'll want to make sure to thinly slice your apples and not make a huge mound — about 2 inches high is enough. Also, make sure to leave about a 2-inch border between the filling and the edge to give you enough crust to fold over your apples, and create some rough pleats here and there to help contain the filling. Remember that the look of this bake is rustic, so nothing needs to be perfect.</p> <p>You can also add other things to your crostata filling to give it a little extra pizzazz, including cranberries, golden raisins, or walnuts. Seasonings like Chinese five-spice can add layers of dimension to your rustic apple crostata, too, and a little liqueur can take this dessert to the next level. You can also replace the apples with other fruits, including pears, to bring an unexpected element to the Thanksgiving table.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2315135/forget-apple-pie-easier-dessert-bobby-flay-recommends-crostata/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9592"> <h2>#9592. How to proof bread in the oven: Common challenge, simple solution.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-09/how%20to%20proof%20bread%20in%20oven.jpg" alt="How to proof bread in the oven: Common challenge, simple solution." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>During proofing, bread and other yeasted doughs do best in a temperature-controlled, humid, draft-free environment. Your kitchen counter may not cut it (especially in colder months), but is there a corner of your kitchen that fits that description? Yes, your oven — and you don’t even need to fire it up!</p> <p>Yeast dough is happiest when rising at temperatures between 75°F and 78°F. It will certainly rise in cooler or warmer temperatures. But for most doughs, that range is optimum for both yeast development and bread flavor.</p> <p>Your oven’s interior will pretty much mirror room temperature. And depending on the time of year (or how much you use air conditioning), that temperature could be pretty cool—too cool for yeast’s comfort.</p> <p>To get the oven up to that ideal proofing temperature, people often turn to a couple of different methods. I decided to try a bunch of them to see which is best — and helpfully, there was a clear winner.</p> <p>It’s tempting to simply preheat the oven for a minute or so to warm its interior; but not only is this hit-and-miss (How long should I leave it on? Will the oven get too hot?), it’s ineffective; the heat quickly dissipates once you turn the oven off.</p> <p>Enter your oven light. When turned on, your oven light’s slow, gentle heat will gradually warm the oven to the desired temperature. After trying a number of different methods for proofing bread in the oven, including several listed below, this was my clear favorite because it created the ideal temperature (not too hot, not too cold), maintained that temperature for several hours, and was essentially failproof (no overshooting the temp, for example!).</p> <p>It can take your oven a while to reach the desired temperature, especially if your kitchen is cold to begin with. With so many variables — season, climate, kitchen, oven — you’ll want to do a simple experiment to determine your own best method for turning your oven into an effective, efficient proof box:</p> <p>Take your oven’s temperature before turning on the light. Then turn on the light and measure the temperature again at 15-minute intervals, to see just how quickly the light warms things up. For reference, the light in my electric oven takes about an hour to raise the oven’s interior temperature by 10 degrees, and another hour to raise it an additional five degrees; your results will probably vary a bit.</p> <p>Warm your oven to about 80°F before turning off the light. Over the next couple of hours, the temperature will gradually drift down by about 10 degrees, giving your rising dough plenty of time in and around that 75°F to 78°F sweet spot.</p> <p>Once you know how to warm your oven using only its lightbulb, think about maintaining humidity: Dry dough can develop a tough skin, which inhibits rising.</p> <p>If you’re proofing dough in a bowl (or later, a shaped loaf in a pan), cover it with a clear plastic shower cap or reusable plastic bowl cover. Whatever you use, make sure it's large enough to form a “poof” on top, so the cover doesn’t touch the rising dough.</p> <p>For shaped rolls (or anything else in a large, flat pan), use an extra-large shower cap; or simply drape the pan with well-greased plastic wrap, waxed paper, or parchment.</p> <p>What if your oven doesn’t have a light, the lightbulb only lights when you open the oven door, or it’s a “cool” LED bulb?</p> <p>Then your best bet is a pan of boiling water set on the lowest rack, which will both warm and humidify your oven’s interior. Place the bread dough on the oven’s middle rack; no need to cover it.  Set a shallow pan (e.g., 9" x 13" pan) on the lower rack, and add four cups of boiling water. Quickly close the oven door.</p> <p>Your oven’s temperature will immediately rise by about 30 degrees, which will probably be warmer than you want. Cool it down by opening the door wide for about five minutes; the temperature should drop about 15 degrees.</p> <p>As the water in the oven cools, the air around it cools, too. But it happens so gradually that your oven should still remain sufficiently warm for the one to two hours your bread typically needs to rise. For longer-rising breads, simply switch out the cool water with another pan of hot water, if necessary.</p> <p>Some ovens actually have a proof setting or proofing drawer. I don’t always love using this setting, though: Most are programmed to temperatures ranging from 90°F to 100°F, far warmer than yeast dough’s optimal 75°F to 78°F. For best results, figure out how long it takes to reach about 80°F, then turn it off.</p> <p>Tip #1: If you have to open the oven door to check your rising dough, don’t worry. Unlike the huge 15- to 20-degree drop you experience when opening a fully heated oven, the temperature inside your light- or steam-warmed oven will only drop by a degree or two.</p> <p>Tip #2: Typically, you don’t preheat your oven with rising dough inside. So when your dough is close to fully risen, remove it from the oven and set it somewhere safe. (If there’s room, the top of your fridge is both warm and out of harm’s way.) Timed just right, your bread will be perfectly proved by the time the oven finishes preheating.</p> <p>Tip #3: To prevent someone from killing your rising dough by turning on the oven (say, to warm their leftover pizza), write “NO!” on a sticky note and affix it to the oven’s start button. Really!</p> <p>For the highly passionate bread baker (or a small baking business), an electronic proof box like the Brod & Taylor Proofer Pro is a step up from proofing dough in the oven. It controls temperature with exquisite precision, from cold-proofing (down to 41°F) for those overnight ferments up to 122°F for an express warmup, all while ensuring perfect humidity. Wi-Fi and programmable timers let you control your dough’s development for up to eight days. It’s literally set it and forget it — the process is simple, but the results are simply amazing.</p> <p>Still looking for a warm, draft-free spot for your rising bread dough? Think beyond your oven to other major appliances: Both your clothes dryer and dishwasher can double as a proof box!</p> <p>Cover photo by Mark Weinberg; food styling by Liz Neily.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>Dough temperature is key to achieving consistently great results in your bread baking.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/23/how-to-proof-bread-in-oven" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9591"> <h2>#9591. Trainn MCP</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p><p> Create product videos and courses from any AI chat </p> <p> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/trainn?utm_campaign=producthunt-atom-posts-feed&utm_medium=rss-feed&utm_source=producthunt-atom-posts-feed">Discussion</a> | <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/r/p/1313622?app_id=339">Link</a> </p></p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.producthunt.com/products/trainn" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9589"> <h2>#9589. Give Boxed Cake Mix A British-Style Upgrade With Cream And One Jarred Ingredient</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/give-boxed-cake-mix-a-british-style-upgrade-with-cream-and-one-jarred-ingredient/l-intro-1794324813.jpg" alt="Give Boxed Cake Mix A British-Style Upgrade With Cream And One Jarred Ingredient" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.</p> <p>Anyone who believes British cuisine falls short has likely never experienced a British cake, with notable example being a traditional Victoria sponge. Much like a classic cup of tea, this dessert represents the essence of British baking, offering elegance through simple ingredients. Even novice bakers can easily prepare one from scratch, but using a boxed cake mix offers a far more convenient alternative. Upgrading a simple store-bought mix into an authentic Victoria sponge requires just one key addition to your pantry: a good jar of strawberry or raspberry jam.</p> <p>Jam is at the heart of a Victoria sponge. The cake consists of two light, fluffy sponge layers sandwiched together with jam and whipped cream. Early versions of this cake, which trace back to Victorian-era afternoon tea culture heavily championed by Queen Victoria, were most commonly filled with just raspberry jam, no cream. Today, however, many bakers include a layer of whipped cream or vanilla buttercream alongside the jam, although traditionalists still debate the "proper" filling.</p> <p>Adding jam to a Victoria sponge sounds simple enough, but there is an art to it. Before assembling the cake, make sure that each sponge layer has cooled completely. This typically takes about 20 to 30 minutes after removing the layers from the oven. If you assemble the cake while it is still warm, the jam (and cream) will melt and run, ruining the distinctive layers that give the Victoria sponge its elegant charm. It is also important to use the right amount of jam — too little will be unnoticeable, while too much will ooze out. A helpful tip is to leave a small border around the outer edge of the bottom sponge so that when the top layer is added, the jam spreads outward without spilling over.</p> <p>The Victoria sponge might be an old-school recipe, but there's always room for improvement. While we'd advocate for experimentation, a Victoria sponge is almost always a golden-yellow sponge. There's no going wrong with a chocolate boxed cake mix, but if you want to keep things traditional (and avoid the wrath of the Brits), it's best to toss a yellow cake mix into your cart. To make life easier, we've already ranked Betty Crocker's Super Moist Yellow Cake Mix as one of the best you can buy.</p> <p>Although a Victoria sponge might sound simple, there are, pardon the pun, levels to this cake. Assembling the sponge is easy enough, but the jam and cream are where you can really let your baking skills speak for themselves. Instead of jarred jam, you could make your own. Sure, it's not as convenient, but your taste buds will thank you. Simply combine diced raspberries or strawberries with lemon juice and sugar, leave it for an hour, then simmer over medium-low heat until it reaches your desired consistency — or consider making a jarringly beautiful ruby red jam. Let it cool completely before spreading, so it doesn't seep into the sponge. Homemade jam will completely elevate your boxed cake mix, and it certainly won't go unnoticed by guests.</p> <p>The cream also offers plenty of room for improvement. The standard approach is a thick layer of homemade whipped cream over the bottom layer, but there are some easy (and more flavourful) upgrades. Whip a few spoonfuls of mascarpone into the cream for a richer, tangier filling, or scrape in some vanilla bean paste, lemon zest, or a splash of elderflower cordial for something brighter. For a nod to a classic British cream tea, swap in clotted cream, which will pair perfectly with the jam. To make clotted cream (because you won't find it in most stores), simmer about three cups of heavy cream with an ounce of unsalted butter until it reduces by half. Chill it overnight, and Bob's your uncle.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2312051/give-boxed-cake-mix-british-style-upgrade-cream-jarred-ingredient/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9588"> <h2>#9588. This Simple Group Activity Cuts Loneliness — Especially For The Most Vulnerable (M)</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.spring.org.uk/images/lonely-3-1.jpg" alt="This Simple Group Activity Cuts Loneliness — Especially For The Most Vulnerable (M)" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Two hours of this activity each week helped reduce loneliness, but some people benefited far more than others.</p> <p>Two hours of this activity each week helped reduce loneliness, but some people benefited far more than others.</p> <p>• Read members-only articles • Adverts removed • Cancel at any time • 14 day money-back guarantee for new members</p> <p>Psychologist, Jeremy Dean, PhD is the founder and author of PsyBlog. He holds a doctorate in psychology from University College London and two other advanced degrees in psychology. He has been writing about scientific research on PsyBlog since 2004. View all posts by Dr Jeremy Dean</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.spring.org.uk/2026/10/group-loneliness.php" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9587"> <h2>#9587. The secret to make-ahead pie crust? Pie crumbs.: Get ahead on your pie baking right now.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/pie%20crumsb.jpg" alt="The secret to make-ahead pie crust? Pie crumbs.: Get ahead on your pie baking right now." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>'Tis the season — to start thinking about holiday baking. And while this time of year is full of joy and celebration, it can also be stressful. We’re all searching for ways to get ahead of the curve, and one of the easiest? Make-ahead pie crust, made using pie crumbs.</p> <p>I first learned of this technique from a 90-something friend with whom I love to talk baking. Over lunch one day, something she said about pie captured my attention.</p> <p>"Did you ever hear of pie crumbs?" she asked. I admitted I hadn't — aside from the obvious: the scraps of pie crust left on the plate after the slice is gone. "My mother used to mix flour and salt and lard together to make this crumbly mixture that she'd store in a crock in the cellar. She called them her pie crumbs. When she wanted to make a pie, she'd just scoop out a few handfuls, add water, and roll out her crust."</p> <p>Sounds like a good make-ahead solution for 100 years ago — but now that we have easy access to freezers, why not just make pie dough and freeze it in ready-to-roll disks? A couple of reasons, actually.</p> <p>1) Pie crumbs allow you to make any amount of crust, from mini apple pies to a crust for a deep-dish 10" pie. With frozen disks, you're looking at a standard single crust — not always exactly what you want.</p> <p>2) Pie crumbs save time. Remove however much of the crumbly mixture you need (more on this below) from the freezer, and within 15 minutes the fat is soft enough that you can add water and roll out your crust. Compare that to the hours it takes to thaw and roll a frozen disk of prepared crust — not to mention the elbow grease if your crust isn’t fully thawed.</p> <p>3) Pie crumbs can be more stable in the freezer than pie crust disks. Why? Because without the added water, no ice crystals form. Ice crystals can damage the flour/water matrix, leading to changes in its structure (which can then potentially lead to changes in your pie crust).</p> <p>Oh, and one other reason I like pie crumbs: If my friend's mother used them, they were probably a 19th-century kitchen time-saver. And I love the feeling of preserving and carrying forward our American baking traditions — even something as simple as a shortcut for pie crust.</p> <p>Choose a standard pie crust recipe: Our Classic Double Pie Crust recipe is good choice, but anything that involves cutting fat into flour (lard, shortening, butter, etc.) will work.</p> <p>Mix flour, salt, and shortening and/or butter: Follow your recipe up until all of the fat is incorporated into the flour. You should be left with a bowl of dry, crumbly dough that barely holds together when squeezed. If using butter, you should be able to see visible chunks scattered throughout the dough.</p> <p>Weigh the pie crumbs: If you’re making a large batch of pie crumbs, it’s helpful to weigh and label the total gram amount so that you can easily remove the amount of pie crumbs for a single pie crust as needed. Our Classic Double Pie Crust makes 488 grams of pie crumbs; that means 244 grams per single pie crust. Label these amounts on your freezer storage bag.</p> <p>Bag, label, and freeze the crumbs: Seal pie crumbs in an airtight, freezer-safe bag and place in the freezer, preferably in the back where it won't be subject to warm air wafting over it each time you open the freezer door.</p> <p>Scoop crumbs out of the bag into a bowl: Whether one crust, two crusts, or one and a half, do the math and measure the crumbs based on your recorded gram amounts.</p> <p>Let the crumbs thaw for 15 to 20 minutes or so: Wait until the butter chunks feel barely pliable in your fingers.</p> <p>Add water and mix: Add water based on your original recipe amount, or just enough water to make a chunky mass when mixed. Squeeze and knead the dough briefly; all you're doing here is bringing the chunks together into one solid piece of dough.</p> <p>Roll the dough, place in a pan, and bake accordingly: From here, your pie crust is the same as any fresh-made crust and can be filled and baked or prebaked for a no-bake filling. (Bonus: Because the crumbs were frozen and remain cold as you work with them, there's no need to chill your rolled-out crust before filling and/or baking.)</p> <p>Fairly indefinitely, though the longer they're frozen, the more chance they have both to absorb freezer odors, and for the fats to start to go off. I've also found that, after about two weeks in the freezer, I need to add a touch more water than usual to bring the dough together — due to the drying effects inherent in freezing.</p> <p>With pie season hard upon us, now's the time to try pie crumbs for make-ahead pie crust. Or maybe you have another old-fashioned pie trick up your sleeve? Share your favorite tips in the comments, below.</p> <p>For detailed ingredient amounts for the crust demonstrated above, see our recipe for Classic Double Pie Crust.</p> <p>And if you're looking for additional time-saving ways to use your freezer in the run-up to the holidays, check out our recipe for Homemade Brown and Serve Rolls and Apple Pie with Make-Ahead Filling.</p> <p>Cover photo and food styling by Liz Neily.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>See our complete collection of Tips and Techniques posts.</p> <p>Top tips from the Things Bakers Know podcast.</p> <p>Mini pies may be the secret to a stress-free celebration.</p> <p>Because we're all wondering what to do with our apple and pumpkin pies.</p> <p>Facebook TikTok Instagram Threads Pinterest LinkedIn YouTube Reddit Substack</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/blog/2026/10/26/make-ahead-pie-crust" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9586"> <h2>#9586. For A Juicier Burger, Make It Scottish-Style</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.foodrepublic.com/img/gallery/for-a-juicier-burger-make-it-scottish-style/l-intro-1794336334.jpg" alt="For A Juicier Burger, Make It Scottish-Style" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Even if you have the perfect blend of meats, some burger patties can stand a little extra moisture to keep them juicy after exposure to high heat. While it may be a less conventional choice, black pudding has a remarkable capacity to make burgers juicier, and the method is actually quite similar to other juicy ground meat recipes.</p> <p>Black pudding is a type of blood sausage consisting of a congealed blend of oats, spices, animal blood, and sometimes assorted organ meats. The use of oats is quite similar to using milk-soaked breadcrumbs in meatballs to keep them moist. When you introduce a bit of black pudding into burgers, the oats can help retain moisture within the patties, keeping them juicy. This helps maintain a consistent level of moisture without adding excess liquid that could inhibit a good crust.</p> <p>While you can always use breadcrumbs or other conventional ingredients instead, black pudding is far meatier and more similar to a patty's flavor profile. Rich in umami and seasonings of its own, it adds so much more than just juiciness. Black pudding can also crisp up on a grill, griddle, or in a pan, so you won't be sacrificing texture for the sake of moisture. Using roughly one part black pudding to two parts meat ensures you can taste both and get a proper level of juiciness, even when using lean blends.</p> <p>Black pudding is something you may rarely encounter in the U.S., and regional varieties can make it difficult to find the perfect one for burger patties. While just about any type can get the job done, texture and flavor profile are important considerations, and you'll have to mix it in properly for the best results.</p> <p>Black pudding isn't monolithic and ranges from the crisped discs served in a full English breakfast to boudin noir in France. The crumbly texture of Scottish black pudding is ideal and makes it easier to add to a burger blend, whether that's beef or another meat mixture. When ingredients are easy to incorporate, it prevents you from overworking the meat and helps you grill burgers like a pro, achieving a tender result that doesn't firm up into a sausage puck. Scottish varieties also make ample use of oatmeal as a binder, so you're more likely to get that juiciness you want.</p> <p>Scottish black puddings also tend to keep the seasonings quite simple, creating something delicious but not overly complex. By focusing on a simple blend of salt, pepper, and aromatics, they leave you more room to season your burgers to your liking. While boudin noir is delicious thanks to its blend of spices like nutmeg, these can easily clash with what's in your seasoning cabinet and make pairings difficult. Simple seasonings also let you add more to your blend, so you don't have to worry so much about ratios.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.foodrepublic.com/2312401/juicier-burger-make-scottish-style-black-pudding/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9585"> <h2>#9585. Does β‑Blocker Use Increase Depression Risk?</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/8/2022/01/pillsg730138337_1448007-e1656645198731.jpg" alt="Does β‑Blocker Use Increase Depression Risk?" style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>The association between β-blocker use and depression was investigated in a population-based observational study recently published in the journal Drug Safety.</p> <p>While depression is often cited as an adverse effect of β-blocker use, there is limited evidence supporting this causal relationship. To better understand the association between beta blockers and the risk of new-onset depression, the study authors analyzed data from the UK population-based Clinical Practice Research Datalink (CPRD) GOLD database.</p> <p>“We identifed patients aged 18-80 years with an incident depression diagnosis between 2000 and 2016, and matched controls, and estimated the risk (odds ratio [OR]) of depression in association with use of β-blockers,” the study authors explained.</p> <p>Findings of the analysis revealed an increased risk of developing depression among short-term users of β-blockers compared with no use at all (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.91; 95% CI, 1.72-2.12).</p> <p>Among short-term users, increased risk of depression was mainly restricted to patients with a neuropsychiatric disorder taking propranolol (aOR 6.33, 95% CI 5.16–7.76).  Patients on propranolol for a cardiovascular indication were found to be at slightly elevated risk of depression (aOR 1.44, 95% CI 1.14–1.82). Apart from propranolol, no other lipophilic β-blocker or hydrophilic β-blocker was found to increase the risk of depression.</p> <p>Additionally, no association was observed between long-term use of β-blockers and the risk of depression (aOR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.85-0.94).</p> <p>“Our findings suggest that the reported association between use of β-blockers and depression may not be causal but rather a result of protopathic bias,” the study authors concluded.</p> <p>Bornand D, Reinau D, Jick SS, Meier CR. β‑blockers and the risk of depression: A matched case–control study. Drug Safety. Published online January 19, 2022. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40264-021-01140-5.</p> <p>Psychiatry Advisor, a trusted source of medical news and feature content for healthcare providers, offers clinicians insight into the latest research to inform clinical practice and improve patient outcomes.</p> <p style="margin-top: 25px;"> <a href="https://www.psychiatryadvisor.com/home/topics/mood-disorders/depressive-disorder/does-%ce%b2%e2%80%91blocker-use-increase-depression-risk/" target="_blank" rel="nofollow noopener" style="color: #0d6efd; text-decoration: none; font-weight: bold;"> → Baca artikel asli </a> </p> </div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> </div> </article> <article class="article-card" id="artikel-9584"> <h2>#9584. Evaporated vs. condensed milk: What's the difference? : Navigating the canned dairy aisle.</h2> <div class="article-body"> <div style="text-align:center; margin-bottom:20px;"><img src="https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/sites/default/files/2026-10/Evaporated%20vs%20Condensed%20milk_Blog_2026_Shot%201_ALT_0045.jpg" alt="Evaporated vs. condensed milk: What's the difference? : Navigating the canned dairy aisle." style="max-width:100%; height:auto; border-radius:8px;" loading="lazy"></div> <div style="text-align:center; margin:20px 0;"> <script type="text/javascript"> atOptions = {'key' : 'f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2','format' : 'iframe','height' : 90,'width' : 728,'params' : {}}; </script> <script type="text/javascript" src="https://upholdbrilliancerecast.com/f9e40eb3b3cd05f1038aac7b36b33ad2/invoke.js"></script> </div> <div class="article-body" style="font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.8; color: #333;"> <p>Navigating the dairy section at the grocery store is one thing, but when it comes to the canned stuff, how much do you know about the difference between evaporated milk and condensed milk?</p> <p>Before we discuss what sets evaporated milk apart from condensed milk, it’s important to discuss their similarities. Evaporated milk and condensed milk are both concentrated liquids made from fresh milk that gets heat-treated until about 60% of the water content is removed. The primary difference between the two is the amount of sugar they contain and their resulting texture.</p> <p>Evaporated milk will typically only contain lactose, or the naturally occurring sugars found in milk and dairy products. Condensed milk, on the other hand, contains around 40 to 45% added sugar. That contrast means condensed milk is much thicker (almost syrupy) and has a more pronounced sweet flavor (it’s no wonder it’s often referred to as sweetened condensed milk!), and evaporated milk runs watery in texture and is lighter in taste.</p> <p>Because of the extreme differences in the sugar content and consistency, evaporated milk and condensed milk cannot be used interchangeably. There will be a very noticeable difference if you use evaporated milk in a recipe that was written to use condensed milk, or vice versa.</p> <p>Using evaporated in a recipe that calls for condensed milk will result in a dessert that is too bland and watery, while using condensed milk in a recipe that calls for evaporated milk can make a dish way too sweet and thick. If your recipe calls for a very small amount (1 to 2 tablespoons) of condensed milk, you could get away with combining a spoonful of evaporated milk mixed with some sugar. But if your recipe needs one whole can of evaporated or condensed milk, be sure to use the correct type.</p> <p>If you want to learn more about – and celebrate – the differences between evaporated and condensed milk, make this Tres Leches Cake, which is a fantastic recipe that utilizes the two milks with heavy cream in a luscious cake soak for dessert. For a different dose of double the milk, you’ll want to try this creamy, custardy Vanilla Bean Flan.</p> <p>Evaporated milk provides richness and creaminess to dishes that are both sweet and savory. It’s often used to enrich custard-based pie fillings, like Hong Kong Egg Tarts, Delicata Squash Pie, and Pumpkin Pie.
